Arch Druid Forms (Levels 11-20)
At 11th level, you gain access to more powerful shapeshifting forms:
Dire Wolf
Pack Tactics: You have advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of your allies is within 5 ft. of the creature and not incapacitated
Bite: 2d6 piercing damage

Howl: As an action, you can emit a frightening howl. Each hostile creature within 30 ft. must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be frightened for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns.
Earth Warden (Dire Bear)
30 temporary hit points while in this form

Earth Slam: As an action, you can slam the ground, causing a shockwave in a 10-ft. radius. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone.
Stone Resistance: You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks
Sky Serpent
Flight speed of 80 ft.
Lightning Bite: Your bite deals 2d8 lightning damage
Glide Reflexes: You gain a +2 bonus to Dexterity saving throws
Ironhorn Ram
AC set to 17 (unless your normal AC is higher)

Charge: If you move at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hit with a ram attack, the target takes an extra 3d6 bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a DC 14 Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 ft. away
Stability: You cannot be knocked prone
Shadow Lynx
Blink: As a reaction when you would be hit by an attack, you can teleport up to 30 ft. to an unoccupied space you can see
Magical Attacks: Your attacks count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks
Druid Circles
Circle of the Land

The Circle of the Land is made up of mystics and sages who safeguard ancient knowledge and rites through a vast oral tradition. These druids meet within sacred circles of trees or standing stones to whisper primal secrets in Druidic. The circle's wisest members preside as the chief priests of communities that hold to the Old Faith and serve as advisors to the rulers of those folk. As a member of this circle, your magic is influenced by the land where you were initiated into the circle's mysterious rites.
Bonus Cantrip
When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice.
Natural Recovery

Starting at 2nd level, you can regain some of your magical energy by sitting in meditation and communing with nature. During a short rest, you choose expended Resonance Points to recover. The Resonance Points can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your druid level (rounded up), and none of the points can be used to cast spells of 6th level or higher. You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
For example, when you are a 4th-level druid, you can recover up to 2 Resonance Points during a short rest.
Circle Spells

Your mystical connection to the land infuses you with the ability to cast certain spells. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain access to circle spells connected to the land where you became a druid. Choose that land, arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, or Murk, and consult the associated list of spells.

Once you gain access to a circle spell, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.
Arctic 3rd level: hold person, spike growth 5th level: sleet storm, slow 7th level: freedom of movement, ice storm 9th level: commune with nature, cone of cold
Coast 3rd level: mirror image, misty step 5th level: water breathing, water walk 7th level: control water, freedom of movement 9th level: conjure elemental, scrying
Desert 3rd level: blur, silence 5th level: create food and water, protection from energy 7th level: blight, hallucinatory terrain 9th level: insect plague, wall of stone
Forest 3rd level: barkskin, spider climb 5th level: call lightning, plant growth 7th level: divination, freedom of movement 9th level: commune with nature, tree stride
Grassland 3rd level: invisibility, pass without trace 5th level: daylight, haste 7th level: divination, freedom of movement 9th level: dream, insect plague
Mountain 3rd level: spider climb, spike growth 5th level: lightning bolt, meld into stone 7th level: stone shape, stoneskin 9th level: passwall, wall of stone
Swamp 3rd level: darkness, acid arrow 5th level: water walk, stinking cloud 7th level: freedom of movement, locate creature 9th level: insect plague, scrying
Murk 3rd level: spider climb, web 5th level: gaseous form, stinking cloud 7th level: greater invisibility, stone shape 9th level: cloudkill, insect plague
Land's Stride

Starting at 6th level, moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.
In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such as those created by the entangle spell.
Nature's Ward
When you reach 10th level, you can't be charmed or frightened by elementals or fey, and you are immune to poison and disease.
Hero Forms: Circle of Thorns
At 10th level, you gain access to the following Hero Druid Forms:
Blight Elk
Aura of Decay: Enemies that start their turn within 5 ft. of you take 1d4 poison damage
Antlers: Your antler attack deals 2d8 piercing damage
Toxic Presence: Plants wither in your presence, and water becomes tainted
Tanglemaw
Bite: Your bite attack deals 2d6 piercing damage and causes the target to be restrained on a failed DC 14 Strength saving throw
Thorny Body: Creatures that touch you or hit you with a melee attack take 1d4 piercing damage
Root Network: You can sense the presence of creatures touching the ground within 30 ft. of you
Nature's Sanctuary

When you reach 14th level, creatures of the natural world sense your connection to nature and become hesitant to attack you. When a beast or plant creature attacks you, that creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your druid spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature must choose a different target, or the attack automatically misses. On a successful save, the creature is immune to this effect for 24 hours.
The creature is aware of this effect before it makes its attack against you.
Circle of the Moon

Druids of the Circle of the Moon are fierce guardians of the wilds. Their order gathers under the full moon to share news and trade warnings. They haunt the deepest parts of the wilderness, where they might go for weeks on end before crossing paths with another humanoid creature, let alone another druid.

Changeable as the moon, a druid of this circle might prowl as a great cat one night, soar over the treetops as an eagle the next day, and crash through the undergrowth in bear form to drive off a trespassing monster. The wild is in the druid's blood.
Combat Shapeshifting

When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you gain Combat Shapeshifting. While transformed by Shapeshifting, you can use a bonus action to expend one or more Resonance Points, regaining 1d8 hit points for each RP expended. Activating Shapeshifting itself still spends a Shapeshifting use, not RP.
Circle Forms

Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Shapeshifting to transform into more powerful beast forms than a typical druid. Your level as a druid determines the maximum CR of the form you can take, as shown in the Druid table.
Primal Strike
Starting at 6th level, your attacks in beast form count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.
Hero Forms: Circle of the Moon
At 10th level, you gain access to the following Hero Druid Forms:
Beastlord (Alpha Animal Hybrid)
Chimera Cub: Your attacks deal 1d4 each of fire, cold, and lightning damage in addition to their normal damage
Alpha Dire Wolf: You can intimidate all creatures within 15 ft. As an action, each creature in range must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute
Pack Leader: Beast allies within 30 ft. of you gain advantage on attack rolls
Mooncursed
Lycanthropic Resilience: You have resistance to all damage except silver
Lunar Rage: During a full moon, your attacks deal an additional 1d8 damage

Howl of the Wild: As an action, you can emit a howl that inspires allies or terrifies enemies. Choose one effect: allies within 30 ft. gain 2d8 temporary hit points, or enemies within 30 ft. must make a Wisdom saving throw or be frightened for 1 minute.
Elemental Shapeshifting

At 14th level, you gain the ability to transform into an elemental. You can transform into an air elemental, an earth elemental, a fire elemental, or a water elemental. You can use this feature twice. You regain expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Circle of the Storm

The Circle of the Storm consists of druids who have forged a special bond with the elemental spirits of storms, lightning, and thunder. These druids are often found in coastal regions, mountain peaks, or anywhere the fury of storms manifests most powerfully. They serve as both harbingers of coming tempests and protectors against their most destructive aspects.
Storm Magic

When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you gain the ability to subtly control the weather around you. If it is raining, you can make it rain harder or stop. If it is windy, you can increase or decrease the wind's intensity. These minor changes last for 1 hour after you stop actively maintaining them.
Additionally, you learn the thunderwave and fog cloud spells, which don't count against your number of druid spells known.
Thunderous Strike
At 2nd level, when you deal lightning or thunder damage to a Large or smaller creature, you can push it up to 10 feet away from you.
Storm's Embrace

Starting at 6th level, you gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage. Additionally, whenever you cast a spell that deals lightning or thunder damage, add your Wisdom modifier to the damage it deals.
Hero Forms: Stormcaller
At 10th level, you gain access to the following Hero Druid Forms:
Tempest Raptor
Lightning Claw: Your claw attacks deal 2d6 lightning damage
Flight: You have a flying speed of 60 ft.
Storm Shroud: You are surrounded by crackling electricity. Creatures that touch you or hit you with a melee attack take 1d6 lightning damage.
Thunderhorn Stag

Charge: If you move at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hit with a horn attack, the target takes 2d8 thunder damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be deafened until the end of its next turn

Thunder Step: Once per transformation, you can teleport up to 30 ft. in a crack of thunder. Each creature within 10 ft. of the space you left must make a Constitution saving throw or take 2d8 thunder damage and be deafened until the end of its next turn.
Weather Sense: You can sense approaching storms up to 24 hours in advance
Eye of the Storm

At 14th level, you gain the ability to create a zone of relative calm within a storm. As an action, you can create a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on you. Within the sphere, winds are reduced to gentle breezes, precipitation stops, and temperature becomes moderate. This effect lasts for 10 minutes and doesn't require concentration.

Additionally, when you cast a spell that deals lightning or thunder damage, you can choose a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one) to automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, taking no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.
Additional Druid Circles
Circle of Thorns

Druids of the Circle of Thorns embrace the darker aspects of nature, decay, poison, and the inevitable cycle of death and rebirth. Often misunderstood and feared, these druids understand that rot and decay are as essential to the natural order as growth and bloom. They tend blighted areas, ensuring that decay serves its purpose without spreading unchecked.
Toxic Affinity

When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you gain resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against being poisoned. Additionally, you learn the poison spray cantrip if you don't already know it.
Blighted Touch

Starting at 2nd level, you can channel decay through your touch. As an action, you can touch a creature and force it to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes 2d6 poison damage and is poisoned until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and isn't poisoned.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Withering Aura

Beginning at 6th level, you emanate an aura of decay. As a bonus action, you can activate this aura, causing nonmagical plants within 10 feet of you to wither and die. Additionally, each creature of your choice that starts its turn within 10 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes 1d6 poison damage.
This aura lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it as a bonus action. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Hero Forms: Circle of Thorns
At 10th level, you gain access to the following Hero Druid Forms:
Blight Elk
Aura of Decay: Enemies that start their turn within 5 ft. of you take 1d4 poison damage
Antlers: Your antler attack deals 2d8 piercing damage
Toxic Presence: Plants wither in your presence, and water becomes tainted
Tanglemaw
Bite: Your bite attack deals 2d6 piercing damage and causes the target to be restrained on a failed DC 14 Strength saving throw
Thorny Body: Creatures that touch you or hit you with a melee attack take 1d4 piercing damage
Root Network: You can sense the presence of creatures touching the ground within 30 ft. of you
Master of Decay

At 14th level, you gain immunity to poison damage and the poisoned condition. Additionally, when you cast a spell that deals poison damage, you can choose a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one) to automatically fail their saving throws against the spell.
Circle of Winterfang

Druids of the Circle of Winterfang have forged a special bond with the harsh beauty and unforgiving nature of winter. These druids often dwell in arctic regions or high mountains, where they serve as guardians of the delicate balance of life that exists in these extreme environments.
Frost Magic

When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you learn the ray of frost cantrip if you don't already know it. Additionally, you learn the ice knife spell, which doesn't count against your number of druid spells known.
Cold Resistance
Starting at 2nd level, you gain resistance to cold damage. Additionally, you are naturally adapted to cold climates, as described in the environmental rules in Chapter 5.
Winter's Embrace

Beginning at 6th level, you can surround yourself with an aura of biting cold. As a bonus action, you can activate this aura, causing each creature of your choice that starts its turn within 10 feet of you to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes 1d6 cold damage and its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn.
This aura lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it as a bonus action. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Hero Forms: Winterfang
At 10th level, you gain access to the following Hero Druid Forms:
Snow Leopard
Claw: Your claw attacks deal 2d6 cold damage
Stealth: You gain a +10 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) checks made in snowy or icy terrain
Frost Walk: You can move across icy surfaces without making ability checks and through snow without penalty
Frost Wyrmling

Breath Weapon: As an action, you can exhale a 30-foot cone of freezing air. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 4d6 cold damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Once you use this breath weapon, you can't use it again until you complete a short or long rest.
Scales of Ice: You gain a +2 bonus to AC
Cold Immunity: You are immune to cold damage
Master of Winter

At 14th level, you gain immunity to cold damage. Additionally, you can cast the control weather spell once without expending Resonance Points, but when you do so, you can only create weather conditions related to winter (such as snow, sleet, or freezing rain). Once you cast the spell in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.
Circle of the Rotshaper

Druids of the Circle of the Rotshaper have formed a unique bond with the often-overlooked creatures of nature, vermin, insects, and other small beings that most consider pests. These druids understand that even the smallest creatures play vital roles in the ecosystem, breaking down dead matter and returning it to the soil.
Vermin Affinity

When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you can communicate simple ideas with tiny beasts such as rats, spiders, insects, and other vermin. Additionally, such creatures are indifferent to you by default rather than hostile.
Swarm Summoning

Starting at 2nd level, you can summon a swarm of tiny creatures to aid you. As an action, you can summon a swarm of insects, rats, or spiders (your choice) in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you. The swarm acts on your initiative count and obeys your verbal commands. It lasts for 10 minutes, until it drops to 0 hit points, or until you dismiss it as a bonus action.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Plague Bearer

Beginning at 6th level, you can infect creatures with debilitating diseases. When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can force it to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature is poisoned for 1 minute. While poisoned in this way, the creature takes 1d6 poison damage at the start of each of its turns.

The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Hero Forms: Rotshaper
At 10th level, you gain access to the following Hero Druid Forms:
Carrion Rat King
Poison Bite: Your bite attack deals 1d8 piercing damage plus 2d6 poison damage. The target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute.
Summon Swarm: As an action, you can summon a swarm of rats that acts on your initiative and obeys your mental commands. The swarm lasts for 1 minute or until reduced to 0 hit points.
Disease Immunity: You are immune to disease and the poisoned condition.
Insect Broodmother

Spawn Swarms: Each time you transform into this form, you can spawn 1d4 swarms of insects (CR 1/4 each) that act on your initiative and obey your mental commands. The swarms last until they are reduced to 0 hit points or until you revert to your normal form.
Chitinous Armor: You gain a +3 bonus to AC
Wall Crawling: You can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without making an ability check.
Master of Vermin

At 14th level, you gain the ability to transform into a swarm of tiny beasts (insects, rats, bats, or spiders) as if using your Shapeshifting feature. While in swarm form, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and you can move through any space large enough for a Tiny creature without squeezing.
Additionally, when you cast a spell that summons or creates beasts, you can choose to summon a swarm instead of individual creatures.
Circle of the Ashen Grove

Druids of the Circle of the Ashen Grove understand that fire, while destructive, is also a natural force of renewal. These druids often tend to areas recovering from wildfires, helping to guide the process of regeneration. They believe that from ash and cinder, new life will always emerge stronger.
Fire Affinity
When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you gain resistance to fire damage. Additionally, you learn the produce flame cantrip if you don't already know it.
Blazing Rebirth

Starting at 2nd level, you can channel the regenerative power of fire. When you or an ally within 30 feet of you takes fire damage, you can use your reaction to grant temporary hit points equal to your druid level + your Wisdom modifier to that creature.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Flame Stride

Beginning at 6th level, you can move through fire without taking damage. Additionally, when you move through a space containing fire, you can choose to leave a trail of fire behind you. Each creature that enters this fire for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes 1d6 fire damage.
The fire lasts for 1 minute or until extinguished. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Hero Forms: Ashen Grove
At 10th level, you gain access to the following Hero Druid Forms:
Charbear
Flame Aura: Creatures within 5 ft. of you take 1d6 fire damage at the start of their turn
Fire Claw: Your claw attacks deal 2d8 fire damage

Smoke Cloud: As an action, you can create a 20-foot-radius sphere of smoke centered on yourself. The area is heavily obscured, and creatures other than you that start their turn in the smoke must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until the start of their next turn.
Blazewood Stag
Flaming Trail: You leave a trail of fire behind you as you move. Each creature that enters this fire for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes 1d8 fire damage.
Burning Charge: If you move at least 20 ft. straight toward a target and hit with a horn attack, the target takes an additional 2d6 fire damage.

Conflagration: Once per long rest, you can explode in a burst of flame. Each creature within 10 ft. of you must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 6d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
Master of Ash

At 14th level, you gain immunity to fire damage. Additionally, when you cast a spell that deals fire damage, you can choose a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one) to automatically fail their saving throws against the spell.

Furthermore, you can cast the plant growth spell to instantly restore vegetation to an area devastated by fire, causing plants to grow to full maturity within minutes rather than over the course of a year.
Playing a Druid

As a druid, you gain power through a profound connection to the natural world and its cycles. Your shapeshifting abilities allow you to literally walk in the paws, hooves, or claws of nature's creatures, gaining not just their physical capabilities but also their perspectives. This intimate understanding of the natural order gives you a unique outlook on the world.
Roleplaying a Druid
Consider these questions when creating your druid character:
What aspect of nature do you feel most connected to? Forests, mountains, storms, or something else?
How did you first discover your ability to shapeshift? Was it a gradual development or a sudden transformation in a moment of need?
What is your attitude toward civilization? Do you see it as a threat to nature or as part of the natural order?
How do you view your role in maintaining the balance of nature? Are you a guardian, a mediator, or something else?
What natural disaster or environmental threat most concerns you, and how do you work to prevent or mitigate it?
Druid Circles in Aethel
In Aethel, druid circles are more than just philosophical groupings, they are actual communities with territories, traditions, and hierarchies. Some notable circles include:
The Verdant Conclave: A powerful circle in the Greenhaven Forest that maintains the ancient groves and protects them from encroachment.
The Stormcallers of Mistral Plains: Druids who ride the great thunderstorms across the plains, bringing rain where needed and diverting destructive weather.
The Frostbound: A secretive circle in the northern reaches who guard ancient secrets frozen in the ice since the Dawn Era.
The Ashen Renewal: Druids who specialize in helping lands recover from devastation, whether natural or magical in origin.
The Deeproot Network: A circle that spans the continent through underground connections, sharing information through fungal networks and root systems.
Druids and Reputation
Your actions as a druid will significantly impact your reputation with various factions:

Nature-Focused Groups: Your fellow druids and other nature protectors will judge you based on how well you maintain the balance. Allowing unnecessary destruction of natural areas will harm your standing.
Settled Communities: Villages and towns near wild areas often have complex relationships with druids, respecting their power but sometimes fearing their priorities.
Arcane Organizations: Many magical academies seek druidic knowledge but approach nature from a more analytical perspective, creating tension.
Religious Orders: Some religious groups view druids as competitors for spiritual authority, while others see them as allies in maintaining divine order.
Druids and Alignment
A druid's alignment often reflects their view of natural order:
Good-aligned druids typically focus on nature's nurturing aspects, protecting life and helping communities live in harmony with their environment.
Neutral druids often embody the balance of nature itself, understanding that both creation and destruction are necessary parts of the cycle.
Evil-aligned druids might emphasize nature's ruthlessness, believing that the strong should dominate the weak as predators do prey.
At 10th level, your Circle and the choices you have made determine which Hero Forms you can pursue. These forms express a philosophy of nature and power rather than an objective moral alignment.
Notable Druid NPCs in Aethel

Thorna Oakenheart - An ancient elf of the Circle of the Land who has protected the Greenhaven Forest for centuries. She appears as a wizened woman with bark-like skin and leaves growing from her hair.
Gale Stormrider - A human Circle of the Storm druid who travels the Mistral Plains, helping communities predict and prepare for the massive thunderstorms that sweep across the region.
Frost Whisperer Narak - A Drakari of the Circle of Winterfang who guards the frozen northern reaches against those who would disturb ancient evils trapped beneath the ice.
Mossbeard - A dwarf of the Circle of the Land who has devoted his life to reclaiming lands corrupted by dark magic, slowly cleansing them and restoring natural growth.
Vex Thornheart - A tiefling of the Circle of Thorns who studies the natural cycle of decay and rebirth, often misunderstood due to her focus on death as part of life's cycle.

engine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Charisma is the Oracle class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Oracle levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Charisma modifier). Revelation attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier. Revelation save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier.

HIT DIE CONFLICT. The class overview registry lists d8, while the detailed Player Rulebook Oracle entry states 6 + Constitution modifier at level 1 and d6 per Oracle level thereafter. This pilot uses the detailed rulebook d6 chassis: 6 + Constitution modifier at Oracle 1 and 1d6 per later Oracle level. The d8 registry value remains a preserved alternative pending owner adjudication.

The Oracle is an exceptional progression class rather than a 25-choice Base/Arch/Hero class. Base Oracle is levels 1-2, Revelation Tier development is the Arch-stage progression at levels 3-9, and Revelation Mastery is the Hero-stage progression at levels 10-20. Mystery and Curse are chosen at level 1 but their later Revelations, Boons and Final abilities remain class-level gated.

Choose exactly ONE Mystery and exactly ONE Curse at Oracle level 1. They are not parallel subclasses that stack. You never gain another Mystery or Curse unless a future explicit retraining or transformation rule says otherwise. Curse limitations are permanent and cannot be removed by ordinary cleansing, curse removal, resurrection or rest.

REVELATION CHARGES are the Oracle's only class power resource. Oracles do not use Resonance Points, spell slots, Weave Dissonance, Overcast or ordinary spell-rank casting for Revelations. Revelation Charges are abbreviated RC. A Revelation card's printed RC cost is paid once before resolution. An illegal activation spends nothing.

RC CAP SCHEDULE for this provisional module: maximum 3 at Oracle levels 1-2, 4 at levels 3-5, 5 at levels 6-8, 6 at levels 9-10 and 7 at level 11+. Increasing the maximum does not automatically refill spent charges except where another feature explicitly says so.

RC RECOVERY. A completed long rest restores RC to maximum. A completed short rest restores 1 spent RC, never above maximum. Each Mystery has exactly one Prophecy Trigger. During a real encounter, your Prophecy Trigger can restore at most 1 RC per round and never above maximum. Trivial enemies, willing staged targets, summoned sacrifices, repeated corpse abuse, copied damage, copied healing and events generated solely to trigger recovery do not qualify.

A single event can satisfy only one Prophecy Trigger recovery for you even if several descriptions could apply. A Revelation repeated or copied by another feature does not independently trigger Prophecy recovery unless that feature explicitly says it counts as a new Revelation use. Restored charges never recursively trigger another recovery.

At Oracle level 11, the preserved registry draft additionally sets your starting RC when a real encounter begins to at least max(3, your Charisma modifier), capped by your current RC maximum. If you already have more RC, keep the higher current value. This encounter-start floor occurs once per encounter and cannot be triggered by staged initiative.

REVELATIONS are divine class techniques, not ordinary spells. Unless a Revelation explicitly says otherwise, magical silence does not prevent a purely mental Revelation, but a Revelation requiring speech, touch, visible symbolism or another listed component obeys that requirement. Revelations do not generate Dissonance and cannot be modified by spell-slot, RP, spell-rank discount or ordinary spell-proc mechanics.

One concentration effect may be maintained at a time unless a specific Oracle feature explicitly creates a narrow exception. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration procedure; if half-damage rounding is required in this pilot, round down. Sustained Revelation control effects grant repeat saves at the cadence printed on the Revelation.

HARD CONTROL GUARD. A creature can suffer at most one Oracle-caused full-turn denial such as Stunned, Paralyzed, Incapacitated by control, or loss of its full Action from your Oracle features per encounter. After that succeeds once, later Oracle effects from you that would fully deny its turn instead remove its Reaction and reduce its Speed to 0 until the end of its next turn after the required save fails.

ADDITIONAL ACTION GUARD. All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. An additional Action cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Features that say a creature acts out of turn use this same cap. Movement-only grants do not count as additional full Actions.

Healing from Oracle features cannot exceed maximum HP, resurrect the dead or remove Wounds unless a feature explicitly says so. Temporary HP never stack. Encounter-only regeneration and drain cannot be farmed outside meaningful combat. Corpse effects create no XP, loot, RC or repeatable corpse resources unless expressly stated.

Copied, echoed, repeated or redirected damage/healing uses only the explicitly copied numeric component. It cannot repeat RC recovery, Prophecy Triggers, action grants, conditions, passive triggers, resource restoration or another copy effect unless the copying feature explicitly says otherwise.

BASE PROGRESSION. At Oracle 1 choose Mystery and Curse; gain the RC engine, Channel Revelation, Prophetic Insight and Divine Sense. At Oracle 2 gain Curse Manifestation, Oracular Trance and Oracle's Burden. No Base feature-selection currency or Skill Points are used.

ARCH-STAGE PROGRESSION. Oracle 3: choose one Tier I Revelation from your Mystery and automatically gain Curse Boon I. Oracle 4: separate ASI or eligible feat. Oracle 5: automatically gain Curse Boon II; any Mystery-specific level-5 feature recorded by the registry belongs to the Mystery module below and does not create an additional generic feature here. Oracle 6: choose one Tier II Revelation and gain Mystery Surge. Oracle 8: separate ASI or eligible feat. Oracle 9: gain your Mystery's fixed Tier III Revelation.

HERO-STAGE PROGRESSION. Oracle 10: gain Curse Boon III and Grand Revelation Foreshadow. Oracle 11: RC cap reaches 7 and the preserved encounter-start RC floor becomes active. Oracle 12: gain the Mystery-specific Mystic Insight. Oracle 13: preserved registry draft grants a second Tier II Revelation; after each completed short rest choose which of your two Tier II Revelations is Attuned for features that specifically refer to an active Tier II option, though both remain known and usable. Oracle 14: separate ASI or eligible feat. Oracle 15: gain Revelation Mastery and Curse Boon IV. Oracle 16: preserved Prophecy Trigger Mastery. Oracle 17: preserved Grand Revelation Foreshadow upgrade. Oracle 18: Prophetic Surge. Oracle 19: separate ASI or eligible feat. Oracle 20: gain the Mystery's Final Revelation and Curse Boon V.

REVELATION MASTERY at level 15 never grants a Revelation you do not know. Choose one mastery enhancement explicitly listed by your Mystery for a Revelation you know. If a listed mastery names a Revelation you did not select, that mastery option is unavailable. Mastery cannot reduce RC below 0, create additional Actions beyond the shared cap or remove repeat-save requirements unless its exact Mystery text says so.

PROPHECY AND DIVINATION never force player beliefs, future choices or confessions. Information features can provide truthful clues, likely outcomes, symbolic visions or current facts, but the Director is not required to reveal unknowable future player decisions. Effects that command or compel a player-controlled character preserve the player's choice of targets and prohibit self-harm, permanent allegiance changes and belief alteration.

CURSE MANIFESTATION provides a common operational intensification rather than ten different hidden sub-engines. When activated, your Curse becomes visibly or metaphysically dominant for 3 rounds: gain +1 on Revelation attacks and +1 to Revelation save DC, but take -1 AC and -1 on your own saving throws for the duration. Any Curse limitation that can normally be voluntarily suppressed cannot be suppressed during Manifestation.

CURSE BOONS are automatic at Oracle levels 3, 5, 10, 15 and 20 for your ONE selected Curse. You do not choose between Curse Boons and do not gain Boons from unselected Curses. Each Curse card below operationalizes all five Boon gates and its permanent limitations.

All class gates use Oracle class level, not total character level. Normal proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. Non-Oracle levels do not raise RC maximum, unlock Curse Boons, Revelations, Mystic Insight, Revelation Mastery, Prophetic Surge or Final Revelation.

INTEGRATION PRECEDENCE. The source ceiling draft conflicts with the registry on short rests and extra Revelation activations. This pilot explicitly chooses 1 RC on a completed short rest and permits a second Revelation only through an expressly granted extra Action or double-cast feature, never more than two Revelation resolutions per round. The preserved ceiling alternative is no short-rest recovery and one activation per round; do not combine both configurations.

All combat-triggered RC refunds, including Prophecy, damage riders and Curse Boons, share ONE recovered RC per round. Rest recovery, encounter-start floor and explicitly limited Final refills are separate. A free, copied or refunded use cannot recursively trigger another recovery. Apply this global cap even if an individual card says its recovery is separate.

The shared Prophetic Surge and your Mystery-specific level-18 Prophecy are two descriptions/options of ONE long-rest use, not two charges. Framework cards such as Tier III, Mystic Insight, Mastery and Final Revelation unlock the named Mystery card and never grant duplicate uses. A level-5 registry Mystery label grants no extra unnamed ability.

Oracle zone default: choose at most three allies and three enemies for each pulse or aura benefit, fixed at activation unless the card names fewer. Persistent damaging/healing zones require concentration and at most three pulses. Pay 1 RC before each pulse after the first, or end the effect; once-per-long-rest Finals include their printed pulses in that limited use. One pulse can affect a creature only once per round. Passive personal resistance and a single-target temporary buff are not zones.

Revelation backlash is the local one-turn penalty of -1 to attacks and saves and -5 feet Speed, ending at the end of your next turn. It is not a level of the general Exhaustion condition. Wound Eater's missed-feeding Exhaustion remains the general condition.

Initiative adjustments change order beginning next round. They never produce or erase a regular turn in the current round; a creature still gets at most one regular turn each round. Ties use the original initiative order. Fixed encounter-start bonuses do not retroactively reorder an encounter.

Extra attacks and echoed damage use base weapon/spell dice before critical-hit extra dice. A redirected damage event cannot be reduced a second time, reflected again or generate RC. Charmed alone does not grant command of a creature's actions.

Oracle’s exceptional ASI/feat schedule is 4, 8, 14 and 19. It does not gain extra ASIs at 12 or 16 from the generic class schedule. The rejected five-milestone draft remains in supersededPlaytestOverrides for traceability.
workedExample: Oracle 5 example: Charisma 16 gives M=3, PB=3 and S=2. The Oracle has maximum RC 4 under the pilot schedule, begins a real encounter at RC4, selected Spiral-Touched as the Curse, and knows one Tier I Revelation costing 1 RC.
Turn 1: use the known Tier I Revelation for 1 RC, so RC4→3. Suppose its Mystery Prophecy Trigger does not occur. Because Revelations use RC only, no RP, spell slot, Burn or Dissonance value changes.

Turn 2: use Curse Manifestation as a Bonus Action for 1 RC, RC3→2. For 3 rounds the Oracle gains +1 to Revelation attacks and save DC but suffers -1 AC and -1 on its own saving throws. The permanent Spiral-Touched limitations continue.

Enemy turn: the Oracle fails a saving throw. Spiral-Touched Curse Boon I is already unlocked at Oracle 3, so once per long rest the Oracle rerolls that failed save and uses the new result. This reroll costs no RC.

Turn 3: Spiral-Touched Curse Boon II is unlocked at Oracle 5. Spend 1 RC to take its once-per-combat out-of-turn Action after another creature finishes its turn, RC2→1. This uses the universal one-additional-full-Action-per-round allowance and cannot generate another extra Action.
After combat, a completed short rest restores 1 RC, RC1→2. A long rest would instead restore the Oracle to the current maximum of4. Neither rest removes the Spiral-Touched Curse.
balanceQuestions: Does the provisional RC cap schedule 3→4→5→6→7, combined with short-rest recovery, Prophecy Triggers and the level-11 encounter-start floor, sustain Revelations without making charge management irrelevant?

Do Curse limitations remain meaningful after their Boons accumulate, especially for Spiral-Touched, Wound Eater, Shattered Mind and False Life, without producing excessive involuntary turn loss or noninteractive penalties?
Do the shared hard-control and additional-Action caps adequately contain Time, Tongues, Shattered Mind and other future Mystery interactions while preserving each Curse's identity?

extraCards.name: Revelation Charges
extraCards.effect: Gain the Revelation Charge resource. Maximum RC follows the pilot schedule: 3 at Oracle1-2, 4 at3-5, 5 at6-8, 6 at9-10 and7 at11+. Long rest restores all RC; short rest restores1. Mystery Prophecy Triggers restore at most1 RC per round in meaningful encounters.

extraCards.name: Mystery
extraCards.effect: Choose exactly one Mystery: Ancestor, Battle, Bones, Cataclysm, Dream, Flame, Life, Shadow, Stars or Time. It determines your Prophecy Trigger, level-1 Mystery identity, Revelation choices, Mystic Insight, Revelation Mastery options, Prophetic Surge variant and Final Revelation. The Mystery cards below define those features.

extraCards.name: Oracle's Curse
extraCards.effect: Choose exactly one Curse from the ten Curse cards below. Its limitations apply immediately and cannot be removed by ordinary magic or rest. Its Boons unlock automatically at Oracle levels3,5,10,15 and20.

extraCards.name: Channel Revelation
extraCards.cost: Use the Revelation's printed RC cost
extraCards.frequency: Whenever a known Revelation is legally usable
extraCards.effect: Channel Revelation is the framework for activating a known Mystery Revelation. Use that Revelation's printed activation, target, range, RC cost, duration, recharge and save/attack procedure. Channel Revelation adds no extra Action or RC cost and cannot be activated without a known Revelation.

extraCards.name: Prophetic Insight
extraCards.duration: Until end of your next regular turn or until used
extraCards.effect: Glimpse several immediate possibilities. Gain advantage on your next attack roll, saving throw or ability check before the end of your next regular turn. You must choose which roll receives the advantage before rolling it. This grants no knowledge of another player's future choice.

extraCards.name: Divine Sense
extraCards.effect: For 1 minute sense the presence, approximate direction and broad nature of divine, undead and extraplanar creatures or active presences within60 feet that are not behind an effect specifically blocking divination. You learn only broad categories such as celestial/divine, undead, fiendish, fey, elemental or other extraplanar, not identity, alignment, statistics or intentions.

extraCards.name: Curse Manifestation
extraCards.effect: Intensify your chosen Curse. For3 rounds gain +1 on Revelation attack rolls and +1 to your Revelation save DC. For the same duration take -1 AC and -1 on your own saving throws. Any part of the selected Curse that can normally be voluntarily suppressed cannot be suppressed while Manifestation lasts.

extraCards.name: Oracular Trance

The Director provides one truthful symbolic vision, omen or useful clue based on information available to the Oracle's Mystery. The trance cannot guarantee another character's future decision or reveal facts that no relevant supernatural source could know.

extraCards.name: Oracle's Burden
extraCards.effect: Your selected Curse is recognized as an intrinsic Oracle class condition rather than an ordinary removable curse. Remove Curse, cleansing, resurrection and similar generic effects cannot remove or suspend it. Only a feature that explicitly names your Oracle Curse can suppress, transform or replace one of its effects.

extraCards.name: Tier I Revelation
extraCards.effect: Choose one Tier I Revelation from your selected Mystery. Tier I Revelations normally cost1 RC unless the Mystery card explicitly says otherwise. You know the chosen Revelation permanently.

extraCards.name: Curse Boon I

extraCards.name: Ability Score Improvement — Oracle 4
extraCards.effect: Choose the campaign's normal Ability Score Improvement option or one eligible feat. This milestone is separate from Revelations, Mysteries and Curse Boons.

extraCards.name: Tier II Revelation
extraCards.effect: Choose one Tier II Revelation from your selected Mystery. Tier II Revelations normally cost2 RC unless their Mystery card explicitly says otherwise. You know the chosen Revelation permanently.

extraCards.name: Mystery Surge
extraCards.rangeAndTarget: One Tier II Revelation you are activating
extraCards.effect: When you activate a known Tier II Revelation, choose one applicable surge: increase its Revelation attack roll or save DC by1 for that use; add S to one rolled damage or healing result; or increase one printed non-concentration duration of 1-2 rounds by1 round. extraCards.name: Ability Score Improvement — Oracle 8

extraCards.name: Tier III Revelation

extraCards.name: Mystic Insight
extraCards.effect: Gain the Mystic Insight printed for your selected Mystery in the Mystery cards below. If that Mystery presents multiple Minor Revelation/passive choices, choose exactly one as specified there.

extraCards.name: Second Tier II Revelation
extraCards.effect: Choose a second Tier II Revelation from your selected Mystery. Both are known and may be used normally. After each completed short rest, designate one of the two as Attuned; only the Attuned option receives features that explicitly refer to your active Tier II Revelation.

extraCards.name: Grand Revelation Foreshadow — Proven Outcome

extraCards.effect: After completing a short-rest prophetic trance, you may later treat one failed Revelation attack roll or Oracle ability check as a success against the required AC or DC. This cannot force another creature to fail a saving throw, override immunity, create a critical hit or bypass an impossible task.

extraCards.name: Prophetic Surge
extraCards.effect: When activating a known Revelation, choose one: reduce that Revelation's RC cost to0 for this use; or, if it has a printed duration of 1-3 rounds, extend that duration by1 round while preserving all normal repeat-save and maintenance cadence. Prophetic Surge never grants an extra Action or bypasses a per-rest use.

extraCards.name: Ability Score Improvement — Oracle 19
extraCards.effect: Choose the campaign's normal Ability Score Improvement option or one eligible feat.

extraCards.name: Final Revelation
extraCards.effect: Gain the Final Revelation printed for your selected Mystery in the Mystery cards below. No Final Revelation from another Mystery is gained.

extraCards.name: Curse Boon V
extraCards.effect: Unlock the Oracle20 Boon printed in your selected Curse card.

extraCards.name: Spiral-Touched
extraCards.effect: LIMITATIONS: your temporal dislocation is obvious in conversation. Once per real encounter, at the start of each of your regular turns until this occurs, roll d20; on1 you lose your Bonus Action and Reaction for that turn as you desynchronize, but retain Action and movement. You have disadvantage on ability checks requiring more than 10 uninterrupted minutes of mundane concentration. BOON I — Oracle3: +3 initiative; 1/long rest reroll one failed save and use the new result. BOON II — Oracle5: resistance to explicitly time/aging damage and advantage on saves against aging/slow effects; once per encounter spend1 RC after another creature finishes its turn to take one additional full Action immediately, subject to the global action cap. BOON III — Oracle10: 1/long rest when damage would reduce you to0 HP without killing you outright, instead regain floor(max HP/4), minimum1, and phase out until the start of your next regular turn; while phased you cannot be targeted, affect other creatures or activate Revelations. BOON IV — Oracle15: once per encounter gain one additional full Action on your turn, subject to the common cap. Also, once per round when an attack hits you, roll d10; on1 it instead strikes a temporal echo and misses. BOON V — Oracle20: 1/long rest as a Reaction before the fourth round of the encounter begins, rewind the current encounter to its initiative-start snapshot: restore combatant positions, HP, temporary HP, conditions, RC and per-encounter uses to that snapshot. Short-/long-rest uses, physical consumables and this Time Loop use remain spent. Slain encounter participants return to their snapshot state and no duplicate XP, treasure or consumables are created. Allies retain memory of the previous timeline. Time Loop does not restore RP, Ki, Conviction, Blood Gauge, device stock, healing reserves or any other daily/rest resource; only the named RC and per-encounter states rewind. No loot changes ownership through rewinding. Record the snapshot at initiative; if no complete snapshot exists, this option is unavailable and unspent. It cannot undo a previous encounter or duplicate a per-rest use.

extraCards.name: Wound Eater
extraCards.effect: LIMITATIONS: HP recovery from rests and from another creature's healing is halved, rounded down; your own Wound Eater drains and your own Revelations are not halved. Before a long rest completes, you must have successfully drained HP from a meaningful hostile living creature since your previous long rest or gain one level of Exhaustion after the rest. Your corpse-like appearance imposes disadvantage on the first friendly social check with an unfamiliar mortal who can clearly see you, unless circumstances make the appearance irrelevant. BOON I — Oracle3: once per turn in a real encounter after your weapon or touch attack damages a living non-construct enemy, pay 1 RC to drain 1d6 HP; you regain half the actual drain rounded down. BOON II — Oracle5: once per round when you reduce a meaningful living hostile to0 HP, regain1 RC; gain resistance to necrotic damage from non-Revelation sources. BOON III — Oracle10: 1/short rest as an Action touch one dying hostile living creature at0 HP; that creature dies and you regain HP equal to one-quarter your maximum HP rounded down. It cannot trigger from summoned, trivial or staged creatures and removes no Wounds. BOON IV — Oracle15: pay 2 RC as a Bonus Action to activate a 10-foot drain aura, requiring concentration for at most three pulses; pay 1 RC before each pulse after the first or end it. You may suppress it freely. During a real encounter, at the start of your turn up to three meaningful living enemies in the aura takes S necrotic damage; regain HP equal to the total actually dealt, capped at S+M per turn. BOON V — Oracle20: 1/long rest as an Action, up to three meaningful living enemies within20 feet lose HP equal to the lesser of one-quarter their maximum HP or Oracle level+M; you regain half the total actual HP lost, capped at one-half your maximum HP. Allies, constructs, undead, trivial creatures and summons are unaffected.

extraCards.name: Soul-Cracked
extraCards.effect: LIMITATIONS: divination that attempts to read your alignment, aura or intent returns inconsistent results unless it specifically overcomes Oracle curses. Once each encounter, before your first damaging Revelation resolves, roll d6: 1 fire, 2 cold, 3 lightning, 4 necrotic, 5 psychic, 6 radiant; that Revelation's damage becomes the rolled type. While subject to a geas, binding oath or magically enforced pact, the first time each turn you knowingly act against its terms you take S psychic damage. BOON I — Oracle3: immune to Charmed effects whose purpose is compulsion or domination; 1/long rest reroll one failed save against another mind-affecting effect. BOON II — Oracle5: once per encounter before a damaging Revelation, spend no additional RC and choose fire, cold, lightning, necrotic, psychic or radiant; change that Revelation's damage to the chosen type. Until it resolves, divination attempting to read your intent returns blank. BOON III — Oracle10: 1/long rest when another creature would Charm or dominate you, negate that effect against you and force the source to make a Wisdom save against your Revelation DC; on failure it becomes Charmed by you until the end of its next turn, with no belief or permanent allegiance change. BOON IV — Oracle15: resistance to psychic damage and +2 on saves against mind-control effects. Divination directly targeting you rolls d2; on1 it returns a contradictory but non-fabricated symbolic result rather than actionable information. BOON V — Oracle20: 1/long rest as an Action end one curse, geas or possession on yourself or one willing ally within15 feet if that effect is not explicitly artifact/plot-locked. If its originator is a creature on the same plane, it makes a Wisdom save, taking 3S d6 psychic damage on failure or half on success.

extraCards.name: Haunted
extraCards.effect: LIMITATIONS: take -2 on Stealth checks in haunted locations or crowded civilized spaces where the attending spirits can manifest. Once per tense social scene the Director may call for a DC10 Wisdom save; on failure a spirit speaks through you and you have disadvantage on your next social check in that scene. Addressing absent or not-yet-present people remains a roleplaying manifestation. BOON I — Oracle3: +1 AC against the first attack made against you each round; 1/long rest when initiative begins, declare the spirits' warning and you cannot be Surprised in that encounter. BOON II — Oracle5: once per encounter when a single-target attack damages you, reduce its damage by 5+Oracle level, minimum0; if any damage is prevented, the attacker makes a Wisdom save or takes -2 on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn. BOON III — Oracle10: while conscious, you and allies within15 feet cannot be Surprised; such allies gain +2 on Insight checks. BOON IV — Oracle15: 1/long rest as an Action, enemies of your choice within15 feet make Wisdom saves; failure causes Dread for up to2 rounds, giving -1 on attack rolls and saving throws. Affected creatures repeat the save at the end of each turn, ending Dread on success. BOON V — Oracle20: 1/long rest summon one spirit scout for10 minutes. It can travel along a route you have personally traveled on the same plane, up to1 mile from you, observe with ordinary sight/hearing, speak with willing dead spirits it encounters and deliver one short prophetic message. On return it truthfully reports what it directly observed and may identify one unexpected creature or person's name it actually encountered. It cannot pass sealed planar barriers, read minds or reveal unknowable facts.

extraCards.effect: LIMITATIONS: unless you suppress the chorus, take -2 on social checks with mortals who do not understand your overlapping speech. You may suppress it as an Action for10 minutes; while suppressed you cannot use Tongues Boons requiring supernatural speech. Prophetic statements may be misunderstood narratively but the Director should not falsify player intent. After more than1 uninterrupted hour of mundane concentration, make a DC10 Wisdom save or lose the final10 minutes of progress to intrusive voices. BOON I — Oracle3: understand all spoken mortal languages and fragmentary divine script; allies within25 feet who can hear your interpretation gain +2 on Lore and Insight checks directly involving that communication. BOON II — Oracle5: once per encounter as an Action, one enemy within15 feet makes a Wisdom save; on failure it would lose its next Action, subject to the Oracle hard-control guard. BOON III — Oracle10: 1/long rest as an Action ask one creature within15 feet a yes/no question. A non-player creature makes a Charisma save; on failure it must answer truthfully with yes, no or 'I don't know.' A player-controlled creature retains agency and may refuse, in which case the Revelation yields 'unclear' rather than compelling speech. BOON IV — Oracle15: 1/long rest communicate meaningfully with beasts, ordinary plants and willing spirits for1 hour. BOON V — Oracle20: 1/long rest as an Action speak one short command of no more than five words to creatures of your choice within30 feet that can hear you. Each makes a Wisdom save. On failure it follows the command until the end of its next turn, subject to the hard-control guard; the command cannot cause direct self-harm, force belief change, permanent allegiance, confession or surrender of essential possessions. A creature that succeeds takes 3S d6 psychic damage instead.

extraCards.name: Burning Blood
extraCards.effect: LIMITATIONS: once per round when slashing or piercing damage deals actual HP damage to you, your blood ignites: you and hostile creatures within5 feet each take1d4 fire damage. You cannot gain cold resistance from a beneficial spell, item or class feature and cold-tagged healing restores0 HP to you. After slashing or piercing damage wounds you, take -2 on Stealth until a creature spends an Action succeeding on DC10 Medicine to bind the wound or you complete a short/long rest. BOON I — Oracle3: gain fire resistance. Once per round when a melee weapon attack deals damage to you, the attacker takes1d4 fire damage. The first time each round your curse blood ignites, hostile creatures within5 feet take1 additional fire damage. BOON II — Oracle5: before activating a damaging Revelation, spend1 RC to ignite it. Add fire damage equal to half that Revelation's unmodified rolled damage dice total, rounded down, minimum1; mundane extinguishing cannot remove ongoing fire riders from that use. Until the Revelation resolves, your curse blood ignition does not damage allies. BOON III — Oracle10: when your blood ignites, allies within10 feet gain +1 damage on their next weapon hit before the start of your next turn. You may spend1 RC when this triggers to extend the burst to15 feet and deal1d4 fire damage to hostile creatures in that area. BOON IV — Oracle15: once per short rest when you first fall below half maximum HP, erupt in a 15-foot fire burst. Enemies make Dexterity saves, taking 2S d6 fire on failure or half on success; you take no damage from this flare. BOON V — Oracle20: 1/long rest as a Bonus Action become a living pyre for3 rounds. At the start of each hostile creature's turn within15 feet it takes S d6 fire damage. Once per your turn when at least one enemy takes fire damage from you, regain1d6 HP, capped at S+M HP per turn. Allies in the aura gain fire resistance and hidden/invisible creatures within10 feet cannot benefit from mundane darkness or visual concealment against creatures illuminated by your pyre.

extraCards.name: False Life

Before a healing spell from another creature restores HP to you, its caster may make Wisdom (Insight) against your Revelation save DC. On success healing works normally. On failure roll d2; on1 the spell restores0 HP to you but still expends its normal costs. Non-spell healing is unaffected. You remain conscious but cannot move, speak, take Actions or Reactions; ordinary undead ignore you unless you attack or otherwise reveal yourself. End the effect voluntarily at the start of your turn. BOON III — Oracle10: 1/long rest when reduced to0 HP without instant death, remain conscious until the end of your next regular turn. During that turn choose either move up to your Speed, speak normally or activate one Revelation; you cannot do more than one of those options. If still at0 afterward, become unconscious normally. BOON IV — Oracle15: resistance to necrotic damage. Once per round when an undead creature hits you with an attack, roll d10; on1 the attack misses instead as it mistakes you for kin. BOON V — Oracle20: 1/long rest when you are at0 HP but not destroyed outright, appear dead until the start of your next regular turn. During that interval you are incapacitated. At the start of your next turn rise with floor(max HP/4), minimum1, and gain necrotic immunity for2 rounds. Undead within15 feet treat you as non-hostile until you damage, control or overtly oppose them. Divination during the apparent-death interval returns one false but plausible state-description you choose; it cannot fabricate events outside your own condition.

extraCards.name: Shattered Mind
extraCards.effect: LIMITATIONS: take -2 on concentration saves. Once per tense social scene, make a DC10 Wisdom save when the Director identifies a meaningful pressure point; on failure you involuntarily speak a brief prophetic fragment, but the player chooses wording that does not reveal protected secrets unless already known. After each long rest make a DC10 Wisdom save; failure gives fragmented memories of others' dreams, a narrative complication with no automatic mechanical penalty. BOON I — Oracle3: once per encounter choose one: move up to your Speed as a Bonus Action without provoking opportunity attacks; or activate one known Tier I Revelation using a Bonus Action instead of its normal Action. If you use the Revelation option, you cannot also take a full Action that turn. BOON II — Oracle5: +2 initiative, roll initiative twice and take the higher, and immunity to Stunned. Pay the second Revelation's normal RC cost but no additional special maintenance charge; normal concentration saves threaten both. At the end of the extension choose one sustained effect to end; starting a third ends the previous two immediately. BOON IV — Oracle15: once per short rest reroll a failed Intelligence or Wisdom ability check and use the new result; gain +2 on Insight checks made to read motives. BOON V — Oracle20: 1/long rest gain one additional full Action during your turn, subject to the universal one-extra-Action cap. The additional Action may only activate a Revelation or be used to Dash/Move as an Action and cannot generate another Action.

extraCards.name: Consumed
extraCards.effect: LIMITATIONS: your body increasingly displays your Mystery and imposes -2 on checks made specifically to disguise or conceal those supernatural alterations without magical assistance. Significant body changes require armor and fitted gear to be refitted during ordinary downtime at the Director's normal maintenance cost; this never destroys attuned equipment. THEME DAMAGE TYPE for this pilot: Ancestor psychic, Battle force, Bones necrotic, Cataclysm thunder, Dream psychic, Flame fire, Life radiant, Shadow psychic, Stars radiant, Time force. BOON I — Oracle3: reduce the first instance of your Mystery theme damage you take each round by PB. Once per long rest suppress visible transformation for1 hour, though divination still detects your Mystery. BOON II — Oracle5: while in light or no armor gain +1 AC. Unarmed strikes and natural weapons count as magical and once per turn deal +1d4 theme damage. BOON III — Oracle10: once on each of your turns add +1d4 theme damage to one weapon or touch attack hit. BOON IV — Oracle15: ignore nonmagical difficult terrain explicitly associated with your Mystery's theme. Allies moving within5 feet behind you during the same round may treat those spaces as normal terrain until the start of your next turn. BOON V — Oracle20: 1/long rest as a Bonus Action fully embody your Mystery for3 rounds. Gain immunity to the theme damage type, +2 on Revelation attack rolls and Revelation save DC, and add S to one Revelation damage or healing roll each turn. Allies within10 feet gain +1 AC. Visible transformation cannot be suppressed during this embodiment.

extraCards.name: Fate-Bound
extraCards.effect: LIMITATIONS: when you voluntarily swear a specific oath or explicitly accept a prophetic obligation in play, record it. Knowingly and voluntarily breaking it costs1 RC if available and deals S d6 psychic damage; if you have0 RC you still take the damage. This never forces you to keep the oath. When the Director presents a clearly identified foreseen disaster that you previously accepted as an omen, deliberately abandoning it without confronting its immediate consequence gives -2 on saving throws until you confront the omen, the omen passes, or you complete a long rest; this is consequence, not compelled behavior. BOON I — Oracle3: 1/long rest before an ally within30 feet makes a check or save tied to a declared party decision, speak an omen and give +2 to that roll. If the party changes plans before the roll, the named ally retains the bonus for the originally described type of challenge until the end of the scene. BOON II — Oracle5: once per encounter after an attack against you is rolled but before damage, force the attacker to reroll and use the new result. BOON III — Oracle10: 1/long rest when an ally within25 feet rolls a natural1 on a saving throw, you may transfer that failed save to yourself if the effect could legally affect you. The ally treats its save as successful; you suffer the failed-save effect as though you were the target, without another save. If the effect cannot legally affect you, the transfer cannot be used. BOON IV — Oracle15: +2 on saves against death effects, banishment, forced temporal/fate displacement and effects explicitly severing a destiny bond. 1/long rest reroll one failed death save. BOON V — Oracle20: 1/long rest before one ally within30 feet makes an attack roll or saving throw, declare the exact successful outcome aloud. That roll automatically succeeds but is not automatically a critical hit. If the ally never attempts the declared roll before the encounter ends, you lose1 RC, minimum0. The prophecy cannot specify impossible secondary consequences, compel target behavior or override immunity.

extraCards.name: Ancestor Prophecy Trigger
extraCards.frequency: At most once per round during a real encounter
extraCards.effect: When an ally benefits from one of your Oracle features and then lands a critical hit before the end of its next turn, regain 1 RC, never above your maximum. One critical event restores at most 1 RC and copied attacks or staged targets do not qualify.

extraCards.name: Ancestral Guardian
extraCards.effect: A spectral guardian accompanies you. Gain +1 AC against the first attack targeting you each round and +1 on saves against charm, fear and other mind-affecting control. Once per long rest when an ally within 3 tiles is targeted by a single-target attack, use your Reaction before the roll; the guardian becomes the target instead and the attack automatically hits the guardian harmlessly, then the guardian vanishes until your next long rest. The interception cannot stop area effects.

extraCards.name: Echo Voice

extraCards.effect: You may communicate telepathically with willing allies within 5 tiles. When one such ally fails an attack roll, saving throw or ability check, use your Reaction and spend 1 RC before another roll is made. That ally rerolls the failed roll with +2 and must use the new result. The reroll cannot itself trigger another Echo Voice.
