## Placement and involuntary endings

A transformation does not grant movement. A voluntary size change keeps the same spatial anchor and must fit before payment. Preserve the existing footprint on a same-size change when possible.

A mandatory ending still occurs if the root anatomy does not fit. First try its normal space at the same position, then a legal squeeze under the [movement rules](COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md). If neither fits, record a placement conflict. The **new provisional placement procedure** permits only a nearest legal adjacent placement in the same unobstructed region. It cannot pass through a wall, closed barrier or occupied space. Choose the minimum displacement that fits the whole body; among ties, preserve the greatest overlap with its previous footprint. If still tied, the Director uses a fixed neutral board order, not a tactical choice by the affected player. If no adjacent candidate fits, the conflict remains until the obstruction is removed or a legal relocation effect resolves it. Do not search farther afield.

This mandatory normalization spends no movement and triggers no opportunity attack, charge distance, movement benefit or other movement rider. It changes no remaining movement allowance and grants no invented crushing damage. It does not permit a voluntary form change to bypass its preflight.

Track actual height and terrain. Losing flight while unsupported starts ordinary falling from the current location; reversion never moves the creature directly to the ground. Ending a burrowing form underground does not move the creature to the surface. Master of Vermin's permission to pass through Tiny gaps changes clearance, not its printed size.

Use the actual space of the expressed anatomy:

| Size | Space | On a grid of 2.5-foot subcells |
|---|---|---|
| Tiny | 2.5 by 2.5 feet | 1 subcell |
| Small | 5 by 5 feet | 2 by 2 subcells |
| Medium | 5 by 5 feet | 2 by 2 subcells |
| Large | 10 by 10 feet | 4 by 4 subcells |

V6 explicitly supplies Tiny and Medium space. Small and Large complete this bounded table provisionally; the supplied V6 passage does not separately list them. Size category still matters even when two sizes occupy the same space. Squeezing changes clearance and its penalties; it does not change size, carrying capacity or weight. Exact Tiny occupancy requires subcells or equivalent measurement, not treating Tiny as Medium.

## Body weight and conditions

**New provisional rule:** a creature-form transformation preserves the body's existing base physical weight unless an exact rule changes it. Size alone does not change weight. A 180-pound character therefore remains 180 pounds as a Tiny Hawk or Large Bear. This is a magical transformation rule, not a claim about the weight of ordinary animals. It applies equally to the current 26 Druid and 12 creature-form spell profiles.

Record base body weight separately from equipment and condition effects. Petrified multiplies current body weight by ten once; it does not rewrite the base weight or multiply repeatedly for multiple applications. Ending or changing a form does not cure that condition. Temporary Druid form ends under its existing Incapacitated rule, then Petrified continues to apply to the reverted body. An anatomy permitted to persist keeps its own base weight and the same condition overlay.

True Polymorph object anatomy uses its actual documented output weight. Its output ceiling remains the lower of current effective input weight and earliest recorded origin weight. Include a current applicable weight-changing condition in the input, but never rebase the origin ceiling upward. Equipment, casualty Load and estimated pounds do not establish material available for a transformation. Creature-origin object anatomy has no independent sale, salvage or harvest value.

For another creature, mount, floor or platform supporting you, count your effective body weight plus all actual equipment in your custody, including melded items, once. For your own inventory capacity, count what you carry, not your own body weight. Conditions change only the items or body their exact rules affect.

## Carrying and Load

Use pounds for actual weight and Load for inventory burden. Extraction Class describes cargo danger and attention. A casualty's Load describes the difficulty of transporting a body; it is not the body's weight. These quantities answer different questions and never convert automatically into each other.

The following is a **new provisional reconciliation** of V6 physical handling with the staged Gameplay Loop inventory rules. It does not promote the historical Gameplay Loop file into the approved books. V6's optional encumbrance variant remains preserved as an alternative; do not add its penalties to this Load procedure.

| Carrier size | Physical carry limit in pounds | Push, drag or lift limit in pounds | Inventory capacity in Load | Casualty Load for a body of this size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tiny | Strength score × 7.5 | Strength score × 15 | Strength score ÷ 2 | 1.5 |
| Small | Strength score × 15 | Strength score × 30 | Maximum of 0 and Strength score − 2 | 3 |
| Medium | Strength score × 15 | Strength score × 30 | Strength score | 6 |
| Large | Strength score × 30 | Strength score × 60 | Strength score × 2 | 12 |

Use the character's current Strength score, not the modifier or an imported monster score. Tiny's Inventory capacity and casualty Load are new provisional additions. The pound limits come from V6; Small, Medium and Large Load values come from the Gameplay Loop. Larger unsupported transport sizes require their own completed rule before this table can handle them.

Keep fractional Loads without rounding. An item with a printed Load uses that value. If it has only a known weight, its **provisional Load is pounds divided by ten**. A Load-only item may use ten pounds per Load as a clearly labeled estimate for ordinary hauling; this is insufficient for effects requiring documented physical mass.

Count a container's own empty Load plus the contents' Loads, unless an explicitly inclusive Load already covers those exact contents. Handle pounds separately: sum the empty container weight and contents' weights, or use an explicitly inclusive gross weight for the contents it covers. An inclusive Load does not make a printed weight inclusive, or vice versa. Apply this rule through nested containers and meld budgets so every item counts exactly once in each quantity.

With positive carried Load at or above half capacity and no greater than capacity, you are **Burdened**: reduce Speed by 10 feet and apply disadvantage to checks to climb, swim or move silently. An empty inventory is not Burdened, including at zero capacity. Above capacity, that inventory cannot be carried routinely; drop or transfer something, or use a legal alternative such as dragging or a vehicle. These threshold and zero-Load details are provisional clarifications.

Apply actual physical limits when handling a known weight. Between physical carry capacity and twice that capacity, pushing or dragging uses the lower of otherwise-current Speed and 5 feet. A Speed of 0 stays 0; a Speed of 3 stays 3. Lifting does not independently permit movement: moving while supporting a weight must satisfy carrying, pushing, dragging or another exact rule. An anatomy restriction, such as Hawk's prohibition on carrying a Medium ally, still applies even if numbers would fit. Burden penalties do not create hands, harnesses, lift or access to melded gear.

Transporting a creature must pass both checks: the carrier can physically handle the body's effective weight and associated equipment, and can accommodate the casualty Load plus the equipment's Load. Petrified multiplies the body weight by ten, not its casualty Load. Removing gear can reduce equipment weight and Load; it cannot reduce the body's weight or erase its condition.

## Meld limits across repeated transformations

**New provisional meld exception:** legally melded gear is excluded from both your transformed body's active Inventory Load and its own active pound-carrying limit. Record its full Load and weight separately while it remains inaccessible. New external equipment uses the expressed form's current capacities and still needs compatible anatomy and custody.

A **continuous meld chain** begins when root anatomy first enters a transformation that melds gear. At that instant, record two fixed ceilings: the pre-transformation body's ordinary active Load capacity and its ordinary physical carrying capacity in pounds. Legally melded gear must fit both. Keep the actual total Load and pounds of the hidden gear, counting containers and contents once in each quantity.

Druid-to-Druid changes, internal Shapechange switches, suppression, permanent True Polymorph and continuous replacement by another spell do not end the chain or increase its ceilings. Later changes to size or Strength neither increase nor retroactively shrink these historical ceilings. An existing item is not expelled merely to make room for a new one.

A later spell replacement may capture an external item only if the whole item fits the remaining room under **both** ceilings. Do not partially meld an item unless its source defines a divisible cargo quantity. A new item that will not fit remains external if compatible with the destination and within its current carrying limits; otherwise drop it or, for a forced resolution without legal placement, record its placement as pending. Excess cargo never grants immunity to a hostile or forced transformation. Druid-to-Druid changes continue to preserve their existing meld and never recapture external cargo.

For a voluntary change, declare and preflight the full item disposition before spending costs. A successful hostile or forced change resolves its mandatory custody consequences without deleting items or refunding its costs. This same overflow procedure applies at the first forced transformation if the target began with excess cargo; only gear within both starting ceilings can become hidden.

When someone else carries the transformed character, count its casualty Load plus both its melded and external equipment Load. Count the effective physical body weight plus all that equipment for actual weight handling. Melding therefore provides no weightless cargo for another carrier.

Only an actual final return to root anatomy, with the hidden equipment released and reconciled, ends the chain. Returned gear rejoins active inventory under the root body's **current** capacities. Resolve excess with the return-and-drop procedure; overload cannot prevent a mandatory reversion. A later new transformation can then establish a new pair of ceilings from its actual legal starting state.

## Extraction Class and Secure Cargo

Extraction Class is a danger and logistics rating, not a carrying allowance:

| Class | Cargo |
|---|---|
| 0 | Ordinary trade goods |
| 1 | Common monster parts or durable salvage |
| 2 | Uncommon, fragile or regulated cargo |
| 3 | Rare artifacts, volatile substances or living captives |
| 4 | Very rare strategic cargo or dangerous curses |
| 5 | Epic cargo likely to attract sovereign or faction intervention |
| 6 | Legendary cargo requiring a dedicated extraction operation |

Retain relevant Fragile, Volatile, Cursed, Living, Contraband, Perishable and Attention tags. A light object can carry a high Extraction Class, and a heavy ordinary crate can remain Class 0.

**New provisional wording for Secure Cargo:** spend an Action on one legal attach, lift, transfer or protective operation involving one discrete cargo unit or bundle with an assigned Extraction Class. The unit must be physically handleable as declared; naming an entire convoy a bundle does not make it one operation. The action grants no extra capacity, hands, equipment, automatic success, invulnerability or reduction in Extraction Class. Apply actual restraints, harnesses, checks, hazards and source-specific handling requirements.

## Examples

**The remote sword.** A Druid wears armor, holds a staff and carries a pack containing two potions. A spare sword is in a wagon. The armor, staff, pack and both potions meld when the Druid changes. The sword remains in the wagon. Neither potion can be consumed from the melded pack.

**A compatible harness.** A transformed creature acquires a harness made for its present anatomy. A later change checks the harness against the destination form. If it does not fit, the voluntary change requires a legal drop. The harness is neither erased nor added to the old melded equipment.

**The crowded hand.** A spell Humanoid acquires and holds a new weapon. When the spell ends, root anatomy can keep that weapon if legal. The original melded weapon returns to an available legal carrying position, or is dropped if necessary. It does not replace or duplicate the new weapon.

**The loaded Hawk.** A Strength 9 Druid becomes Tiny with 3 Load of legally melded gear. It stays inaccessible and uses neither of the Hawk's active carrying capacities. Tiny capacity is 4.5 Load and 67.5 pounds. An additional package of 3 Load and 30 pounds in a genuinely compatible external carrying arrangement fits both capacities, but exceeds half the Load capacity of 2.25 and makes the Druid Burdened. A rescuer carrying that Hawk counts 1.5 casualty Load plus all 6 Load of equipment, totaling 7.5 Load, and separately satisfies the full body and equipment weight.

**The repeated replacement.** A Strength 9 Medium character starts a chain with 8 Load and 80 pounds of legal gear. The fixed ceilings are 9 Load and 135 pounds. The remaining hidden capacity is therefore 1 Load and 55 pounds. A later spell cannot hide a new 3-Load, 30-pound package even if the current form can carry it externally. A whole 0.5-Load, 50-pound item fits both remaining ceilings; a 0.5-Load, 60-pound item fails the pound limit. Changing form or casting again does not refresh either ceiling.

**The stone casualty.** A Medium ally has a documented base weight of 180 pounds and becomes Petrified. The body now weighs 1,800 pounds but still contributes 6 casualty Load. A Strength 18 Medium rescuer can normally carry 270 pounds or push, drag or lift 540 pounds, so cannot move that body alone through these ordinary procedures, even with enough spare Load capacity. Additional gear is counted separately.

## Source decisions and implementation status

The [first body and equipment conference](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_BODY_EQUIPMENT_CONFERENCE.md) supplies the equipment procedures. The [additional exact evidence](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/CODEX_TEMPORAL_CARRYING_EVIDENCE.md) and [GPT's completed reconciliation](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_CARRYING_RECONCILIATION.md) preserve the V6, Gameplay Loop and Core conflicts and their dispositions. The corrected candidate above replaces the first conference's full-cell Tiny footprint, factor-four mass proposal and automatic active Load from melded equipment. The manuscript review's chain budgets, pound exemption, borrowed-custody correction, separate inclusive quantities and neutral placement tie rule are applied here. [GPT confirmed this exact revised manuscript and its six examples](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_BODY_FINAL_AND_ABJURATION_CONFERENCE.md); the [review manifest](BODY_EQUIPMENT_REVIEW_STATUS.json) records its scope.

The current Druid helper does not yet update the shared body, equipment custody or geometry. The spell helper's coarse hands check does not implement the full compatibility procedure. The finite ground-plane temporal helper does not model elevation, burrowing or Tiny subcells. The authored rules and these implementation gaps are separate; none of them enables full Time Loop or closes the whole-game review.

# Create and advance a character

**REVIEWED CHARACTER FOUNDATION — authored operational PLAYTEST candidate.** The [source conference](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CHARACTER_FOUNDATION_CONFERENCE.md) and [exact review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CHARACTER_FOUNDATION_EXACT_REVIEW.md), with both requested wording repairs applied, settle the class foundations and advancement rules below. Use the [17-class tables](CHARACTER_FOUNDATION_TABLES.md) beside this guide. Use the later reviewed ancestry/background and equipment guides for their stated scopes, and the reviewed language chapter for language grants and records. Remaining option dependencies and live companion parity are still separate work.

## Begin a character sheet

1. **Record the concept and first Base class.** Choose one of the 17 classes. Start at character level 1 and that class’s level 1. Keep a chronological level record and the order in which you enter classes. Arch and Hero are later stages within a class, not additional Base classes. The former Fighter/Swashbuckler entries and separate historical prestige records supply no extra starting class or automatic grants.
2. **Generate six abilities.** Choose the method before generating scores: roll four d6, discard the lowest and total the other three, six times; or assign the standard array 15, 14, 13, 12, 10, 8. Assign those six results once to STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS and CHA. Keep the original rolls. Do not reroll, mix methods or select a preferred set without a separate table rule. The optional provisional point-buy method below is also available.
3. **Record ancestry and any required variant.** Apply its actual ability increases once after assigning scores, resolving an OR choice once. Record size, movement, senses, languages and each complete trait procedure from its source. Trait names alone are insufficient. Do not stack alternative builder/racial-variant entries onto the same book trait. Use the reviewed ancestry/background integration and complete source bindings for all14 base ancestries and45 variants; apply the reviewed language chapter to their actual language grants. This step grants no authority to revise their cosmology or origin lore.
4. **Choose one background.** Record its actual skills, tools, languages, feature and starting package, including required choices. Use the reviewed ancestry/background guide and complete source bindings for the20 background packages; its named outstanding interfaces remain outstanding. The source permits a custom background with two skills, two tools/languages, equipment and a Reputation-related feature developed with the Director; that permission does not supply an invented unlimited feature or a second background.
5. **Apply starting training.** Use this first class’s saves, armor, weapons, tools and number of skill choices from the foundation tables. Use the class list for each skill choice. Add ancestry/background training with the duplicate procedure below. Proficiency grants training, not equipment ownership, spells or a second PB on one roll.
6. **Set HP, Hit Dice and proficiency.** First-character-level base HP is the maximum face of this class’s HD; add current CON modifier, minimum 1. Record one unspent Hit Die of that size. At level 1 PB is +2. Keep base maximum HP separate from later effects, reductions and systemic multipliers.
7. **Acquire the actual class kit.** Follow the class’s own level-1 engine, automatic grants and scheduled choices. Ordinary classes start with four Base choices, at least two active, where their schedule says so. Druid, Oracle and Paladin have explicit schedules; follow those instead. Make required engine/path choices, such as Oracle Mystery and Curse, exactly when their cards require them. Use the [class library](CLASS_PLAYTEST_INDEX.md), [legal acquisition examples](CLASS_PLAYTEST_BUILD_EXAMPLES.md), and [Paladin oath pairs](PALADIN_OATHS_AND_OATHBREAKERS.md). No legacy Skill Points, companion feature strings or historical prestige rows add grants to this schedule.
8. **Record magic and class resources.** Use the class’s current Core V2 RP table and rank gates, plus its actual known/prepared/spellbook procedure. Record each selected operational spell’s identity and casting class. Enough RP never unlocks a rank or school. Oracle uses Revelation Charges; Soldier and Warrior have no general RP casting. Initial class resources and empty stores follow their actual engine setup; preparation or copying is not waived. Read [shared class rules](CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md) and [spell integration](SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md).
9. **Choose starting equipment or money.** Take the class and background packages, **or** roll the first class’s starting wealth and buy equipment with it. Wealth replaces all starting package equipment, including package money; background training and features remain. Record purchases, remaining coins, ammunition, components, containers, quantities and actual weight/Load. An item must exist with usable statistics; a proficiency or feature label cannot create it. Use the reviewed equipment/acquisition guide, complete item procedures and starting-package records; keep any actually unresolved entry visible.
10. **Finish the derived sheet.** Calculate ability modifiers, trained saves and skills, legal equipped AC, movement, weapon attacks, class attacks/DCs and actual resource caps. Choose one applicable AC formula rather than adding formulas. A normal proficient attack is d20 + PB + its actual attack modifier; class DC is 8 + PB + its actual class modifier. Use actual negative modifiers; the class card’s minimum-1 effect modifier is not a minimum attack/DC modifier. Note conditions, Wounds, supplies and other scene state separately. Record the source/card for every nonordinary number.

An ancestry/background feature, spell or item that remains mechanically unresolved is a visible unfinished dependency. A checked box or a saved companion character does not resolve that dependency.

## Abilities and training

Ability modifier = floor((score − 10) / 2), including negative results. For example, 8 gives −1, 13 gives +1 and 16 gives +3.

**Optional new candidate method:** 27-point buy, scores 8–15 before ancestry. Costs are 8:0, 9:1, 10:2, 11:3, 12:4, 13:5, 14:7, 15:9. Spend no more than 27 points across six scores; no score outside that range. This adopts the existing companion method as a provisional option, not a claim that the book already specified it.

Resolve duplicate training as follows:

- For a selectable grant, choose another eligible option from that grant’s own list.
- For a fixed ancestry/background skill grant with no alternative list, choose another of the 20 basic skills.
- For a duplicated tool, choose another eligible tool from that grant’s list; if it has no list, use another actually supported tool in the same broad category.
- Duplicate armor, weapon, save or multiclass chassis training gives no skill or feat compensation. A new multiclass skill selection must still use its own permitted list.
- Duplicate proficiency never creates Expertise unless an exact feature says so. If a proficiency grant requires a choice and every legal option for that grant is already possessed, that grant provides no additional proficiency. Character creation, multiclass entry or advancement remains legal. Do not substitute a feat, Expertise, another category of proficiency, an unrelated skill/tool, or a banked future selection. This applies to skill and tool lists, including a legal replacement list or category that is itself exhausted.

PB is applied once to a check even if a skill and tool both qualify. An exact Expertise multiplier modifies that one proficiency contribution; it does not add another independent PB.

## Gain a level

Opening campaigns officially use milestones. The Director’s announced milestones grant advancement; a CR-to-XP UI helper is not the official Opening reward law. The book’s cumulative XP thresholds remain available for tables using optional XP. See [XP provenance](XP_ADVANCEMENT_CANON.md).

Each earned advancement adds one total character level, to a combined maximum of 20. Choose one existing Base class to advance, or enter one new Base class if eligible. Process multiple earned levels one at a time; do not skip intervening choices.

1. Record the gained class and new class level. Recalculate total level and PB: +2 at total 1–4, +3 at 5–8, +4 at 9–12, +5 at 13–16, +6 at 17–20.
2. Add one new unspent Hit Die of the gained class’s size. Previously spent Hit Dice remain spent; gaining this die does not refresh any earlier die. For HP, roll that die or use its fixed rounded-up average: d6→4, d8→5, d10→6, d12→7. Record the base result before CON. This includes taking a new class’s first level after character level 1; maximum first-level HP is never granted again.
3. Apply exactly the gained class’s acquisition row, automatic improvements and class-level prerequisites. Complete its choices and any newly reached Arch/Hero gate. Automatic grants, scheduled selections and ASIs are distinct; do not pay a selection twice or grant an extra selection because the same feature appears in a legacy table.
4. At an ASI milestone, increase one score by 2 or two scores by 1, normally no higher than 20, or select one eligible operational feat. Ordinary milestones are class levels 4/8/12/16/19; Oracle uses 4/8/14/19. Follow any already-reviewed specific exception. No starting feat or repeatable feat is implied. [Eight complete feat options](FEAT_PLAYTEST_INDEX.md) do not make the other 327 complete.
5. Update legal repertoire, prepared capacity, class scaling and resource maxima at the gained **class** level. Use class-specific Druid preparation, Wizard spellbook/matrices and other explicit rules before generic acquisition defaults. New capacity does not provide an unnamed spell, an unearned choice, a filled Echo record or an extra prepared spell without the required preparation procedure.
6. Recompute base maximum HP from all attained-level records using current CON: sum(max(1, each stored base value + current CON modifier)). Then apply the separate [maximum-HP ledger](MAXIMUM_HP_PLAYTEST.md), including compatible bonuses, reductions and systemic factors. Do not feed an already modified maximum back in as the base.
7. Keep current HP and spent resources unchanged except for a downward clamp when a maximum falls. An ordinary level-up is not healing or a rest: it cannot revive a downed/dead character, erase Wounds or refill already spent Hit Dice, RP, RC, class pools, item charges or uses. Newly granted features still follow an explicit acquisition/initialization clause if they have one; “gain a maximum” alone does not mean “restore current.”

**New HP completion:** each level’s HP contribution has a minimum of 1. Recompute those individual floors after permanent CON changes. This preserves retroactive CON adjustment without a naive level×modifier-change formula that can bypass a floor. Capacity increases grant no current HP; decreases can clamp current HP without damage/healing triggers, consistent with the reviewed maximum-HP interface. Temporary ability effects follow their own actual source rules rather than being silently treated as permanent advancement.

No banked card selections, free retraining or free respec is introduced. Use an existing explicit replacement/retraining procedure where one exists.

## Multiclass entry and class features

When entering a new Base class, meet the multiclass score prerequisites for **every held class and the new class**. The foundation tables give the exact source gates; a class’s descriptive primary ability is not a substitute. These requirements are checked on new-class entry. Losing a qualifying score later does not erase earned classes/features, though it can prevent entering another new class. Advancing a class already held is not a new-class entry test.

Only the first character class grants its full starting saves and proficiency package. Each later newly entered class grants its separate multiclass proficiency row once. It grants no second background, starting wealth/equipment or full starting skill count. Its genuine level-1 engine/features and acquisition schedule still apply.

**New chassis clarification:** a level-1 card whose sole function is to restate starting armor/weapon proficiency cannot bypass the multiclass table. Paladin Martial Proficiency therefore supplies no heavy-armor bypass. An independent non-chassis mechanic in a feature remains available on its actual terms.

Use the largest equivalent Extra Attack count, never their sum. Use one applicable AC formula, never their sum. Duplicate historical Channel Divinity labels do not manufacture another use pool. Distinct operational class engines and paid techniques remain distinct and obey their own costs and the shared action limits.

Class level controls rank access, acquisitions, S scaling, Arch/Hero gates and finales. Total character level controls PB and optional XP thresholds. A Bard 5 / Mage 5 is total 10 with PB +4, but neither class has reached its Hero gate.

## One shared RP pool

Calculate each eligible class’s own current candidate RP pool at its own class level. Sort these classes by:

1. Caster tier: Full (Cleric, Druid, Mage, Wizard), then Half (Paladin, Ranger), then Hybrid (Bard, Shaman, Mirrorsage, Crimson Agent), then Minor (Dragoon, Monk, Thief, Tinker).
2. Within a tier, higher class level first.
3. If class levels tie, higher actual RP pool first.
4. If both tie, the class acquired earlier first. Record that order; do not choose a different primary per cast.

Oracle, Soldier and Warrior contribute no RP pool. Maximum RP = the first class’s full pool + ceil(one quarter of the second class’s pool). With only one eligible class use its pool; with none, maximum RP is 0. Third and later eligible classes contribute no extra capacity, while retaining their earned class features and legal repertoire. Use current Core V2 candidate pools, not the older smaller companion-derived tables.

All RP-paid spells and techniques use this one merged pool unless an exact rule names another resource. RC, BG, Momentum, Ki, Conviction, Lay on Hands and other class resources remain separate. A change in the primary class or maximum is not recovery: preserve current RP and clamp only if above the new maximum. This can reduce maximum RP when a newly entered higher-tier class becomes primary; do not silently choose a larger lower-tier pool instead.

Each ordinary cast declares its casting class before costs. That class must independently know/prepare the spell, meet its school/rank gate and supply its own casting ability. Another class’s levels or repertoire cannot fill those requirements. Where two classes know the same spell, choosing its casting class does not create a second spell identity.

## Shared strain, recovery and concentration

Keep one character-wide Dissonance number and one Refrain history across classes. For a cast, evaluate limit = max(4, 2 + total-character PB + max(0, the actual casting-class modifier)). Apply the existing surcharges, ranked-cast cutoff, repetition and explicit class exceptions from [shared class rules](CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md). Switching casting class does not clear either history; the same spell identity still repeats. Class cadence benefits require their actual ownership and trigger conditions. Idle decay and Grounding occur once per character turn, not once per class.

Generic Retune happens once per eligible completed short rest for the character. It restores max(0, round-half-up(maximum RP / 4) + the current primary RP class’s casting modifier), capped at the merged maximum, and clears Dissonance. Optional once/day meditation uses that same primary class’s positive modifier and the existing PB-based strain reduction. Long-rest RP recovery restores the merged pool under the existing recovery rules. None of these generic procedures duplicates because the character has more classes or recovers a different named resource without its own rule.

Oracle Revelations use RC and do not generate ordinary Weave strain unless expressly stated; they do not clear existing strain/Refrain from another class. One ordinary concentration slot is shared across classes, with only the exact already-reviewed linked-effect exceptions such as Spell Tether, Tethered Cast and Crimson Harmony. No generic Overcast option is reintroduced.

## Worked foundation checks

- **First Bard level:** CON 14 gives modifier +2; base HP 8+2 = 10, one d8 Hit Die and PB +2. Choose three class skills from the 20-skill list and four eligible Base cards with at least two active, as the Bard schedule directs. Background/ancestry grants remain separate and must be fully specified before play.
- **Bard 1→2 without a rest:** fixed HP base 5 and CON +2 increase base maximum 10→17. If current HP was 6 it stays 6. The second Bard level grants its actual two Base selections. A higher RP maximum does not refill spent RP.
- **New class does not repeat maximum HP:** a Bard 3 taking Mage 1 adds d6 roll or fixed 4, plus CON; it does not add 6 merely because Mage is class level 1. Total PB is still +2 at character level 4. The character must meet Bard CHA 13 and Mage INT 13 before entry.
- **Retroactive CON with floors:** a d6 first level recorded as 6 and a later d6 roll recorded as 1 give contributions 4 and 1 at CON 6 (−2), total 5. At CON 8 (−1) they give 5 and 1, total 6. Adding a naive two levels × +1 would incorrectly give 7.
- **A three-class caster:** Cleric 6, Druid 6 and Wizard 1 use Cleric/Druid as the two Full-tier contributors because class level precedes pool size. Their own level-6 pools are 15 each, giving 15+ceil(15/4) = 19 RP; earlier acquisition breaks their tie. Wizard 1 adds no RP but retains its own legal Wizard 1 spell access. Total 13 supplies PB +5; no class has a Hero gate.
- **Different casting stats:** at total level 6, PB +3, a modifier +3 caster has limit 8 and a modifier +1 caster has limit 6. Shared Dissonance 6 is below the first limit but at the second. Casting through the second class uses its surcharge; the shared strain number and spell repetition history survive the switch.
- **Monk wealth:** rolling 5d4 for a total of 12 gives 12 gp, not 120 gp. No background-package money is added if this money method replaces the packages.
- **Later Paladin:** a non-Paladin’s entry uses the Paladin multiclass row. Its level-1 Martial Proficiency restatement grants no extra heavy armor or second set of saving-throw proficiencies.

The [reference checks](CHARACTER_FOUNDATION_VALIDATION.json) verify selected calculations and source preservation. They do not execute a live character builder, certify every acquisition interaction or replace human playtesting.

## Source decisions and remaining work

The foundation uses reviewed active class contracts first, then detailed class entries, the Classes Table as fallback and companion data only for actual gaps. The [source evidence](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/CHARACTER_FOUNDATION_SOURCE_EVIDENCE.json) retains every disputed chassis entry, original skill list and source hash. All original books, legacy UI data and class cards remain unchanged.

New candidate decisions are explicitly identified: missing class skill lists, Oracle’s starting Arcana substitution, Tinker’s Engineering option, bounded favored/blade weapon choices, optional point buy, duplicate-grant resolution, per-level HP floors and capacity-only advancement, precise multiclass entry/chassis rules, final RP tie-breaking and shared strain/recovery interpretation. These are authored playtest rules rather than approved-book rewrites.

Next dependencies are the remaining selectable-content and named ancestry/background/equipment interfaces, feat acquisition, remaining spells, the expedition-to-Haven loop and final joint flow review. Broader runtime, balance and publication remain separate. Cosmology stays untouched until after the authorized GitHub push has succeeded and its remote commit is verified.

preparedExcerpts.exactText:
## One shared RP pool

Calculate each eligible class’s own current candidate RP pool at its own class level. Sort these classes by:

1. Caster tier: Full (Cleric, Druid, Mage, Wizard), then Half (Paladin, Ranger), then Hybrid (Bard, Shaman, Mirrorsage, Crimson Agent), then Minor (Dragoon, Monk, Thief, Tinker).
2. Within a tier, higher class level first.
3. If class levels tie, higher actual RP pool first.
4. If both tie, the class acquired earlier first. Record that order; do not choose a different primary per cast.

Oracle, Soldier and Warrior contribute no RP pool. Maximum RP = the first class’s full pool + ceil(one quarter of the second class’s pool). With only one eligible class use its pool; with none, maximum RP is 0. Third and later eligible classes contribute no extra capacity, while retaining their earned class features and legal repertoire. Use current Core V2 candidate pools, not the older smaller companion-derived tables.

All RP-paid spells and techniques use this one merged pool unless an exact rule names another resource. RC, BG, Momentum, Ki, Conviction, Lay on Hands and other class resources remain separate. A change in the primary class or maximum is not recovery: preserve current RP and clamp only if above the new maximum. This can reduce maximum RP when a newly entered higher-tier class becomes primary; do not silently choose a larger lower-tier pool instead.

Each ordinary cast declares its casting class before costs. That class must independently know/prepare the spell, meet its school/rank gate and supply its own casting ability. Another class’s levels or repertoire cannot fill those requirements. Where two classes know the same spell, choosing its casting class does not create a second spell identity.

preparedExcerpts.heading: Shared strain, recovery and concentration
preparedExcerpts.exactText:
## Shared strain, recovery and concentration

Keep one character-wide Dissonance number and one Refrain history across classes. For a cast, evaluate limit = max(4, 2 + total-character PB + max(0, the actual casting-class modifier)). Apply the existing surcharges, ranked-cast cutoff, repetition and explicit class exceptions from [shared class rules](CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md). Switching casting class does not clear either history; the same spell identity still repeats. Class cadence benefits require their actual ownership and trigger conditions. Idle decay and Grounding occur once per character turn, not once per class.

Generic Retune happens once per eligible completed short rest for the character. It restores max(0, round-half-up(maximum RP / 4) + the current primary RP class’s casting modifier), capped at the merged maximum, and clears Dissonance. Optional once/day meditation uses that same primary class’s positive modifier and the existing PB-based strain reduction. Long-rest RP recovery restores the merged pool under the existing recovery rules. None of these generic procedures duplicates because the character has more classes or recovers a different named resource without its own rule.

Oracle Revelations use RC and do not generate ordinary Weave strain unless expressly stated; they do not clear existing strain/Refrain from another class. One ordinary concentration slot is shared across classes, with only the exact already-reviewed linked-effect exceptions such as Spell Tether, Tethered Cast and Crimson Harmony. No generic Overcast option is reintroduced.

# Enchantment control integration — provisional playtest

REVIEWED PROVISIONAL MANUSCRIPT. These NEW integration rules accompany seven approved rank-two Enchantment cards. The [exact review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ENCHANTMENT_RANK2_EXACT_REVIEW.md) approves the submitted body and records the binding interpretations below. Source originals remain preserved. This is not runtime certification, human balance approval, whole-game closure or GitHub delivery approval.

## Ordinary compelled Attack Actions

When an actual compulsion orders an ordinary Attack Action, use the target's native ordinary attack sequence, including inherent Extra Attack and an NPC's native Multiattack if that is actually its ordinary Action. No additional Action/attack is granted. A source expressly limited to one attack retains that limit: Confusing Flash is such an exception. An ordinary attack instruction is not permission to invent an Attack Action or convert another source's single attack into Multiattack.

Spend required ordinary ammunition normally. The command cannot activate consumable magic, special ammunition with a distinct expendable feature, RP/spellcasting, charges, recharge/per-rest abilities or optional finite-resource riders. Actual optional expenditures remain optional and cannot be compelled indirectly by choosing a method which requires them. Where instruction wording leaves the choice open, the target/controller may use a different legal ordinary method. If none satisfies the instruction, that instruction fails without spending a prohibited resource or manufacturing one. Existing source-specific limits and actual absolute prohibitions remain.

## Application IDs and independently scoped components

Each cast has a distinct application ID. Each component retains its own exact source/caster/target, application identity, deadline and actual defense state. Replacing one component never silently replaces another.

For Dire Charm, successfully established Charmed replaces only that caster's previous Dire Charm Charmed relation. Successfully established servant control replaces only the existing Dire Charm servant component across casters. Charmed-only and servant-only casts can therefore coexist. A successful repeat save, expiry or removal clears only still-active components originating from that application; an old application's save cannot remove a replacement component from another cast. Empty applications have no remaining save schedule. Core Charmed from other sources is unaffected. Shared hard-control history never refunds, even if a component is suppressed or replaced before acting.

## Compelled budget arbitration

This NEW rule resolves collisions among actual active mandatory instructions, including Command, Confusing Flash, Illusive Commands, Dire Charm and Crown of Madness. It does not create commands, extend duration, add repeated control to a one-turn source, grant new target permissions or override an explicit source-specific exception.

Record a priority timestamp for each specific instruction:
- Command, Confusing Flash and Illusive Commands: successful establishment of that failed-save instruction.
- Dire Charm and Crown of Madness: issue of that turn's particular valid order, not the age of the underlying spell alone.
- Simultaneous instructions: underlying effect application order, then a stable source/mechanical ID as the neutral tie-break. Record it before resolving choices; do not decide a favorable order after outcomes.

At execution, gather still-active mandatory instructions and consider earlier priority first. A currently impossible/ineligible instruction claims no budget; proceed to the next. Compatible requirements can share one genuine legal execution. A single Action satisfies two instructions only if that same Action actually fulfills both. Once an earlier valid instruction claims an indivisible ordinary Action/interaction, an incompatible later instruction receives no second copy. Movement uses only the actual remaining movement allowance; sequencing instructions cannot reset spent movement or violate an earlier still-maintained posture/restriction.

A losing ongoing instruction is ineffective only for its contested budget/opportunity, not automatically dispelled. Its compatible independent portions may still operate within existing permissions. Its own endpoint, replacement and saves remain. Priority loss never refunds hard-control history. An invalid later order cannot erase an earlier mandate merely by being issued.

Example: Grovel and an Attack Action may both be satisfied if Prone uses only legal movement/posture and the attack remains legal. Two incompatible ordinary Actions cannot both be demanded from one Action budget. This arbitrates actual compelled behavior; it does not make compulsion optional or restore unavailable actions.

## Six-second control cadence outside initiative

This NEW cadence binds Dire Charm and Crown of Madness's ongoing order/end-save procedures. Other sources retain their actual timing unless expressly bound by a further review.

For a target with no existing initiative/control cycle, successful outside-initiative application begins a six-second virtual target cycle: first START immediately after resolution, first END six elapsed seconds later, then repeated six-second cycles. END resolves before the next cycle's START at the same boundary. Maximum duration remains the original absolute60-second deadline; expiry can end the spell before a later opportunity.

Reviewed procedure: a target shares one active virtual control cycle and one ordinary behavior budget across concurrent control applications. A new application during an already-open virtual cycle does not replay START or replenish budgets; its specifically allowed current-cycle END save still occurs. Each spell retains its own maximum deadline, components and saves. This treats application during an outside-initiative cycle like application during an existing regular turn, preventing repeated casts from creating extra immediate Actions.

The cycle supplies the bound spells' order opportunities, one ordinary six-second behavior budget where needed, and their repeat saves. It does not refresh encounter Reactions, recharge, resources, limited uses or manufacture extra combat turns. If actual combat order becomes necessary, establish ordinary initiative before any not-yet-committed hostile behavior; a virtual cycle is no permission for an extra pre-initiative attack.

Reviewed procedure for entering initiative: map the currently open virtual cycle to the target's first actual regular turn. Carry already received order opportunities and spent ordinary Action/movement/interaction budgets into that turn; do not replay or refill them at its START. The next still-unresolved END save occurs at that actual turn's END. Thereafter use actual regular starts/ends for future triggers. Keep the original absolute duration deadline. Do not replay already resolved virtual events. Existing effects begun in initiative retain their ordinary original virtual-marker rules if they later leave it; this bridge is for these effects first established outside initiative.

Application after an actual regular START grants no order for that already-started turn. A source explicitly permitting an affected current-turn END save still grants that save. Extra turns do not add order opportunities or repeat saves.

## Fixed-zone eligibility history

Calm Emotions and Zone of Truth have fixed spherical centers and require actual exposure/line of effect from that center. Geometric presence behind total cover is not yet eligible exposure. When cover opens around a creature still inside, that moment counts as its first eligible exposure.

Keep one save/acceptance result per creature per spell application:
- Calm Emotions: willing acceptance or the actual WIS save at first eligible exposure.
- Zone of Truth: the actual CHA save at first eligible exposure.
- Success: unaffected by that cast for its remainder, including later entry/cover changes.
- Acceptance/failure: the cast's existing effect is active only while exposed inside its zone; leaving or total cover suppresses it, and restored exposure resumes it without another save.

Acceptance is not a freely toggled dispel choice. Independent zones retain separate casters, concentration, histories and deadlines. Identical restrictions or suppression do not add numerical magnitude. Being unaffected by one zone does not make a creature immune to a different cast.

Calm Emotions suppresses actual Frightened effects, including a newly acquired Frightened source. Create and retain underlying records, ordinary clocks, maintenance and scheduled repeat saves. Once no valid suppressor remains, still-existing effects resume without replaying their original application. A condition which independently expires or is cured while suppressed does not return.

No emotion-themed name automatically disables a class ability. Actual Mooncursed, Momentum Rampage, Divine Fury, Fury of the Host and Beast Empathy source cards have no new emotion-maintenance requirement here. Their real Frightened rider on an affected recipient remains subject to suppression; other printed effects continue.

## Scope and open evidence

The instruction-priority, split-component and zone histories above are authored tabletop procedures, not executed stateful engine implementations. Concurrent outside-initiative applications and the first real turn's carried budget have exact manuscript approval; executable runtime integration remains open. Human testing remains necessary for multiple-attack compulsion, long control without concentration, fear suppression and the unchanged Zone of Truth class-price discrepancy.

## Binding interpretations from the exact review

One-shot Command, Confusing Flash and Illusive Commands do not gain a new repeating cadence from this overlay. If their compelled behavior falls into the same current six-second/regular-turn opportunity, their demands compete for the same actual remaining behavior budget through Compelled Budget Arbitration.

Ordinary actual regular-start processing still happens at the first real regular turn: Reaction refresh, recharge, death-save and start effects follow their normal combat rules. Only the Enchantment control START/order opportunity and already-spent ordinary behavior budget are not replayed. The virtual START was not itself a combat turn or resource-refresh event.

For Illusive Commands, an independently valid soft movement/interaction component that survives a blocked hard Action component establishes a new instruction and replaces the prior pending same-spell record. A saved-against, wholly invalid or wholly blocked instruction establishes no replacement.

A Dire Charm application keeps its repeat saves while at least one of its original components remains. Once it has none, its save schedule stops; an old save never removes a later application's replacement component. No hard-control history is refunded.

Command's Grovel does not inherently consume the ordinary Action. Its required Prone posture can coexist with another legal Action. Confusing Flash's Attack branch continues to spend the ordinary Action on exactly one ordinary attack.

# Rank-three Enchantment integration — provisional playtest

REVIEWED PROVISIONAL MANUSCRIPT. This accompanies eight approved rank-three Enchantment cards. The [exact review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ENCHANTMENT_RANK3_EXACT_REVIEW.md) approves the submitted mechanics and marked completions. The existing [Enchantment control integration](ENCHANTMENT_CONTROL_INTEGRATION_PLAYTEST.md) remains authoritative in its approved scope. This approval does not certify runtime, human balance, whole-game closure or GitHub delivery. Cosmology remains outside this work.

## Dominate Beast: independent creatures and companion execution

NEW explicit binding: a Beast with an actual independent regular turn receives Dominate Beast orders at future regular STARTs, after ordinary start processing. Outside initiative it uses the reviewed shared six-second virtual control cycle. It shares the same actual budget with coexisting Dire Charm/Crown orders rather than creating another cycle. It has no repeat ending save, so virtual/real ENDs do not create one. Application after the current START grants no retrospective order. Existing ordinary real-start events still occur on entering initiative; already-received control orders/spent behavior budgets do not replay. The original maximum deadline remains.

A dominated Beast using the reviewed owner-attached companion chassis receives no independent turn. At its existing original owner's regular attached companion phase, the dominator may consciously issue a mental order for that opportunity. No extra caster Action/Bonus Action is charged. Actual Dominate Beast control must still exist, the companion must still be eligible and the command must obey its source profile and resource/behavior limits. Without a valid domination order, an already-valid owner command may execute, otherwise only ordinary uncommanded defensive behavior remains.

The forced execution occupies the ORIGINAL OWNER's shared command allowance for that numbered round and, if damaging/offensive under the existing chassis, its shared offensive allowance. These are structural caps; no unwilling owner's Bonus Action, RP or optional feature is charged. The dominator receives no new companion ledger. If another execution already consumed the command allowance, no extra commanded execution is created. If offense is unavailable but the command allowance remains usable, only a legal nonoffensive command can execute. An ordinary owner instruction is not a magical mandatory instruction and has no compulsion-priority timestamp; a valid domination order supersedes a contradictory owner instruction. An owner's already-paid Bonus Action is not refunded.

Reviewed completion — pending commands: redirecting a still-pending command for THIS SAME companion at THIS SAME attached phase reuses that existing execution's structural command reservation; it is not a second command. A still-pending offensive reservation on that same execution can cover the redirected ordinary attack; no duplicate offensive charge. If an existing reservation lacks offense, a new offensive redirection requires the still-free original-owner offensive allowance. Redirecting to a nonoffensive behavior does not refund an already-consumed/reserved offensive allowance. A reservation belonging to another companion, an already-completed execution or another phase cannot be stolen/reused to create this execution. Existing source-specific explicit release rules retain their scope; domination itself grants no refund.

Reviewed completion — phase availability: this bridge uses only a phase that the actual existing companion lifecycle supplies. It does not manufacture an owner phase after that lifecycle no longer permits one, duplicate it on an extra turn, or assign the companion the independent-Beast virtual control cycle. If no ordinary companion execution sequence is active and a commanded combat act matters, establish ordinary initiative with the source owner's existing companion phase. Noncombat work uses only the existing chassis's actual ordinary permissions and finite structural caps; the spell supplies no unbounded off-screen attack/action loop. Missing phase means no commanded execution, while concentration and absolute deadline continue. These bounded completions have exact manuscript approval.

The original companion profile, source-owner stat/DC rules, bond, ownership, slots, HP, Load, upkeep, summon duration, recharge and limited uses remain. Do not restore the original wild animal's discarded attack profile or substitute dominator levels/DC for its attack statistics. The spell's own INT application save uses its actual caster's spell DC. A phase checkpoint supplies no new regular START/END, Reaction refresh, death save, recharge or periodic/duration tick.

NEW exact completion: independent Dominate Beast casts retain separate applications and concentration. At a shared order opportunity their actual mandatory orders use Compelled Budget Arbitration, with timestamp at each order's issue and neutral same-time application/source order. A valid order never duplicates the actual creature/companion budget. Ordinary owner commands remain outside magical priority arbitration. No hard-control history is refunded if another instruction wins or an existing cap prevents execution.

## Hypnotic Pattern: atomic initial application

NEW spell-specific initial resolution:

1. Choose the perceived legal center using actual class-school range: Enchantment 60 feet, Illusion 30 feet; cube extends 15 feet on each axis.
2. Snapshot all creatures inside with actual center line of effect and actual sight of the pattern. Include self/allies when eligible; no selective omission.
3. Resolve each initial WIS save and determine each failed target's independently legal Charmed/Inc components and hard-control allowance.
4. Apply every target's determined initial components and immediate consequences. Actually applied Incapacitated ends that target's applicable existing concentration normally.
5. If the caster's own Incapacitated ends concentration on this Pattern, queue this Pattern's concentration teardown until every snapshotted target has received its initial application. Then remove all still-maintained components from this cast.

No target is skipped merely because it comes later in an implementation loop. Immediate loss of another target's unrelated concentration remains a real consequence even if Pattern then collapses. This is not a universal simultaneous-area or delayed-condition rule. It creates no late application for an initially prevented component.

Helper rousing ends one selected cast's Pattern application on one creature, removing both that cast's remaining Charmed and Incapacitated components. When a helper cannot distinguish multiple actual Pattern sources, use stable application order to select one, without revealing hidden source/caster metadata. Unlike ordinary Sleep's explicit shared wake, one Action does not rouse all Patterns. Positive post-defense/pre-temp-HP damage ends each actually affected Pattern application under its own damage trigger; it does not retroactively change the waking attack's hit/crit.

Recasts form independent sources under actual concentration transitions. An ordinary caster's old concentration ends before a new cast resolves; only a real multiple-concentration feature permits coexistence. Every new Incapacitated attempt checks hard history; independently legal Charmed may remain when hard control is blocked. Charmed-only applications gain no new repeat save. No general illumination, concealment, Speed 0 or ongoing entry aura is created by the persistent visual pattern.

## Terrifying Gaze and Slow: ending-save clocks

NEW explicit binding: Terrifying Gaze and both Slow modes have regular-target-END repeat saves, including an affected current regular turn's upcoming END. This save cadence is distinct from their maximum-duration endpoint. Extra turns grant no extra ending save.

If Terrifying Gaze begins outside initiative, ending saves occur at original application +6, +12 and +18 seconds; its maximum remains +18. An otherwise legally established Slow begun without a target initiative sequence uses ending saves every six seconds after application until its original 60-second maximum. This grants no new outside-sequence Transmutation Reaction trigger.

Reviewed completion — shared END-only cadence: unlike a commanded behavior cycle, these save schedules supply no START/order or action budget. On entering initiative, preserve already-resolved saves and the original absolute maximum. The first still-unresolved save opportunity maps to the target's next actual regular END, then actual regular ENDs supply future saves; never replay a resolved END or add an immediate transition save. If the deadline precedes that next END, expiry ends the effect first. Effects established in initiative retain their original regular/virtual markers on later exit under existing timing rules. This is the explicitly reviewed narrow transition for these new END-only schedules.

Temporary suppression of a condition/rider never pauses the underlying duration or scheduled saves. An actual successful save ends only that source's application on that target, not another independent cast.

## Slow: mode-specific commitments and overlap

Enchantment and Transmutation are separate actual class-school packages. One casting never receives their union. Both retain rank 3/base 5 RP and the preserved per-class level gates.

Transmutation's Reaction window occurs on a perceived creature's own actual turn, including an extra turn, at the beginning of a distinct voluntary movement segment or an Action after commitment and before the first movement step/main outcome. Moving, taking an Action and resuming movement creates distinct segments; choosing another square during continuous movement does not. Each foot/tile is not a trigger. The triggering creature MUST be selected and up to five additional legal perceived creatures may be chosen.

A valid committed Slow is independent of its parent. If a nested legal interruption removes the parent Action, the paid spell still resolves against still-legal chosen targets; it neither refunds nor cancels/revives that parent. The surviving parent continues after LIFO interrupts. Recalculate remaining movement before its next expenditure using actual current Speed and the unchanged spent-movement ledger. A no-Reactions rider bars future commitments only; a Reaction already legally committed in the stack is not canceled by that rider.

Enchantment's one-Action ceiling counts full Actions already committed on that actual turn. It blocks a future commitment once one is already committed, while an already-committed second Action finishes. Each actual extra turn has its own ceiling; the source grants no extra turn. Actual extra-Action resources may exist but cannot be newly committed contrary to the active ceiling. Bonus Actions, Reactions, movement and inherent attacks inside one legal Attack Action remain.

The Enchantment DEX rider is exactly -2 Dexterity ability checks/saves EXCEPT initiative; it changes no score/modifier, attack, damage, spell DC or unnamed derived value. AC gets its separate -2 only. Half-Speed uses existing strongest-adverse-Speed arbitration against the shared pre-control Speed, followed by the existing later systemic multipliers. Actual narrowly scoped defenses can suppress/block one component without erasing the others. Neither an Action ceiling retaining the ordinary Action nor Reaction denial claims whole-Action hard control.

Each source keeps its own concentration/save/deadline. Same Slow half-Speed/-2 AC/-2 DEX riders do not add magnitude. Distinct active Enchantment/Transmutation riders can coexist through separate casts; ending one exposes whichever other sources remain, not a merged permanent package.

## Suggestion: task scope and hard-control reservation

NEW binding: Suggestion's persistent mandatory instruction uses its successful establishment timestamp for Compelled Budget Arbitration. It retains that priority while genuinely active, but never supplies an extra budget or overrides an earlier applicable absolute restriction. Actual task permissions and reasonable legal details remain as authored on the card.

If the stated task necessarily requires whole ordinary Actions, including after an awaited conditional trigger, establish and claim the hard component once when Suggestion establishes. Do not reserve afresh per later Action. When blocked, only an independently meaningful legal soft task can establish. That surviving task may replace a prior Suggestion; an attempt with no legal meaningful task does not.

A task established without hard control cannot acquire it dynamically. If changed circumstances require an unreserved whole Action, seek an achievable reasonable path within the original soft permissions, such as waiting for an ordinary door opening. If none remains, end the remaining compulsion. Ordinary temporary delay/inconvenience is not itself cancellation. Neither caster nor target/controller may reword the task to create a new hard permission or extend its original eight-hour deadline.

An actually reasonable hostile task can direct the target's actual ordinary Attack Action/native attack sequence and required mundane ammunition; it does not compel optional finite features, special expendable ammunition, spells/RP or other forbidden expenditures. Reasonableness uses actual target beliefs/loyalties/knowledge/circumstances after payment without a caster diagnostic. Bonus Actions, Reactions and separately granted extra Actions are not commandeered. No repeating control cycle is added outside initiative.

## Scope and open validation

The companion pending-command/phase completions, independent Dominate Beast same-spell records, END-only transition, and Mental Chains voluntary-transport/plane completions on its card have exact manuscript approval. The Hypnotic Pattern batch is spell-specific. All prior 229 operational card records and actual source/class files remain unchanged. These are authored procedures, not executed scheduler or companion-control implementations. Human tests remain required for four-target Stunned, sustained native attacks, area Incapacitated, eight-hour Suggestion, no-repeat-save Fear and six-target Reaction Slow.

## Mental Chains: binding separated-plane interpretation

If a creature is involuntarily moved away from an application's anchor plane, that application's voluntary-distance/plane restriction has no effect while the creature remains separated. Ordinary rules govern further travel from that other plane, including voluntary travel elsewhere or return to the anchor plane. Concentration and the original deadline continue. On return, that application's original fixed anchor and boundary resume immediately. Another independent Mental Chains application on the creature's current plane still retains its own actual restrictions. This is the exact review's interpretation of the approved separation/resumption procedure, not a cosmology ruling.

# Rank-three Enchantment integration — provisional playtest

REVIEWED PROVISIONAL MANUSCRIPT. This accompanies eight approved rank-three Enchantment cards. The [exact review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ENCHANTMENT_RANK3_EXACT_REVIEW.md) approves the submitted mechanics and marked completions. The existing [Enchantment control integration](ENCHANTMENT_CONTROL_INTEGRATION_PLAYTEST.md) remains authoritative in its approved scope. This approval does not certify runtime, human balance, whole-game closure or GitHub delivery. Cosmology remains outside this work.

## Dominate Beast: independent creatures and companion execution

NEW explicit binding: a Beast with an actual independent regular turn receives Dominate Beast orders at future regular STARTs, after ordinary start processing. Outside initiative it uses the reviewed shared six-second virtual control cycle. It shares the same actual budget with coexisting Dire Charm/Crown orders rather than creating another cycle. It has no repeat ending save, so virtual/real ENDs do not create one. Application after the current START grants no retrospective order. Existing ordinary real-start events still occur on entering initiative; already-received control orders/spent behavior budgets do not replay. The original maximum deadline remains.

A dominated Beast using the reviewed owner-attached companion chassis receives no independent turn. At its existing original owner's regular attached companion phase, the dominator may consciously issue a mental order for that opportunity. No extra caster Action/Bonus Action is charged. Actual Dominate Beast control must still exist, the companion must still be eligible and the command must obey its source profile and resource/behavior limits. Without a valid domination order, an already-valid owner command may execute, otherwise only ordinary uncommanded defensive behavior remains.

The forced execution occupies the ORIGINAL OWNER's shared command allowance for that numbered round and, if damaging/offensive under the existing chassis, its shared offensive allowance. These are structural caps; no unwilling owner's Bonus Action, RP or optional feature is charged. The dominator receives no new companion ledger. If another execution already consumed the command allowance, no extra commanded execution is created. If offense is unavailable but the command allowance remains usable, only a legal nonoffensive command can execute. An ordinary owner instruction is not a magical mandatory instruction and has no compulsion-priority timestamp; a valid domination order supersedes a contradictory owner instruction. An owner's already-paid Bonus Action is not refunded.

Reviewed completion — pending commands: redirecting a still-pending command for THIS SAME companion at THIS SAME attached phase reuses that existing execution's structural command reservation; it is not a second command. A still-pending offensive reservation on that same execution can cover the redirected ordinary attack; no duplicate offensive charge. If an existing reservation lacks offense, a new offensive redirection requires the still-free original-owner offensive allowance. Redirecting to a nonoffensive behavior does not refund an already-consumed/reserved offensive allowance. A reservation belonging to another companion, an already-completed execution or another phase cannot be stolen/reused to create this execution. Existing source-specific explicit release rules retain their scope; domination itself grants no refund.

Reviewed completion — phase availability: this bridge uses only a phase that the actual existing companion lifecycle supplies. It does not manufacture an owner phase after that lifecycle no longer permits one, duplicate it on an extra turn, or assign the companion the independent-Beast virtual control cycle. If no ordinary companion execution sequence is active and a commanded combat act matters, establish ordinary initiative with the source owner's existing companion phase. Noncombat work uses only the existing chassis's actual ordinary permissions and finite structural caps; the spell supplies no unbounded off-screen attack/action loop. Missing phase means no commanded execution, while concentration and absolute deadline continue. These bounded completions have exact manuscript approval.

The original companion profile, source-owner stat/DC rules, bond, ownership, slots, HP, Load, upkeep, summon duration, recharge and limited uses remain. Do not restore the original wild animal's discarded attack profile or substitute dominator levels/DC for its attack statistics. The spell's own INT application save uses its actual caster's spell DC. A phase checkpoint supplies no new regular START/END, Reaction refresh, death save, recharge or periodic/duration tick.

NEW exact completion: independent Dominate Beast casts retain separate applications and concentration. At a shared order opportunity their actual mandatory orders use Compelled Budget Arbitration, with timestamp at each order's issue and neutral same-time application/source order. A valid order never duplicates the actual creature/companion budget. Ordinary owner commands remain outside magical priority arbitration. No hard-control history is refunded if another instruction wins or an existing cap prevents execution.

## Hypnotic Pattern: atomic initial application

NEW spell-specific initial resolution:

1. Choose the perceived legal center using actual class-school range: Enchantment 60 feet, Illusion 30 feet; cube extends 15 feet on each axis.
2. Snapshot all creatures inside with actual center line of effect and actual sight of the pattern. Include self/allies when eligible; no selective omission.
3. Resolve each initial WIS save and determine each failed target's independently legal Charmed/Inc components and hard-control allowance.
4. Apply every target's determined initial components and immediate consequences. Actually applied Incapacitated ends that target's applicable existing concentration normally.
5. If the caster's own Incapacitated ends concentration on this Pattern, queue this Pattern's concentration teardown until every snapshotted target has received its initial application. Then remove all still-maintained components from this cast.

No target is skipped merely because it comes later in an implementation loop. Immediate loss of another target's unrelated concentration remains a real consequence even if Pattern then collapses. This is not a universal simultaneous-area or delayed-condition rule. It creates no late application for an initially prevented component.

Helper rousing ends one selected cast's Pattern application on one creature, removing both that cast's remaining Charmed and Incapacitated components. When a helper cannot distinguish multiple actual Pattern sources, use stable application order to select one, without revealing hidden source/caster metadata. Unlike ordinary Sleep's explicit shared wake, one Action does not rouse all Patterns. Positive post-defense/pre-temp-HP damage ends each actually affected Pattern application under its own damage trigger; it does not retroactively change the waking attack's hit/crit.

Recasts form independent sources under actual concentration transitions. An ordinary caster's old concentration ends before a new cast resolves; only a real multiple-concentration feature permits coexistence. Every new Incapacitated attempt checks hard history; independently legal Charmed may remain when hard control is blocked. Charmed-only applications gain no new repeat save. No general illumination, concealment, Speed 0 or ongoing entry aura is created by the persistent visual pattern.

## Terrifying Gaze and Slow: ending-save clocks

NEW explicit binding: Terrifying Gaze and both Slow modes have regular-target-END repeat saves, including an affected current regular turn's upcoming END. This save cadence is distinct from their maximum-duration endpoint. Extra turns grant no extra ending save.

If Terrifying Gaze begins outside initiative, ending saves occur at original application +6, +12 and +18 seconds; its maximum remains +18. An otherwise legally established Slow begun without a target initiative sequence uses ending saves every six seconds after application until its original 60-second maximum. This grants no new outside-sequence Transmutation Reaction trigger.

Reviewed completion — shared END-only cadence: unlike a commanded behavior cycle, these save schedules supply no START/order or action budget. On entering initiative, preserve already-resolved saves and the original absolute maximum. The first still-unresolved save opportunity maps to the target's next actual regular END, then actual regular ENDs supply future saves; never replay a resolved END or add an immediate transition save. If the deadline precedes that next END, expiry ends the effect first. Effects established in initiative retain their original regular/virtual markers on later exit under existing timing rules. This is the explicitly reviewed narrow transition for these new END-only schedules.

Temporary suppression of a condition/rider never pauses the underlying duration or scheduled saves. An actual successful save ends only that source's application on that target, not another independent cast.

## Slow: mode-specific commitments and overlap

Enchantment and Transmutation are separate actual class-school packages. One casting never receives their union. Both retain rank 3/base 5 RP and the preserved per-class level gates.

Transmutation's Reaction window occurs on a perceived creature's own actual turn, including an extra turn, at the beginning of a distinct voluntary movement segment or an Action after commitment and before the first movement step/main outcome. Moving, taking an Action and resuming movement creates distinct segments; choosing another square during continuous movement does not. Each foot/tile is not a trigger. The triggering creature MUST be selected and up to five additional legal perceived creatures may be chosen.

A valid committed Slow is independent of its parent. If a nested legal interruption removes the parent Action, the paid spell still resolves against still-legal chosen targets; it neither refunds nor cancels/revives that parent. The surviving parent continues after LIFO interrupts. Recalculate remaining movement before its next expenditure using actual current Speed and the unchanged spent-movement ledger. A no-Reactions rider bars future commitments only; a Reaction already legally committed in the stack is not canceled by that rider.

Enchantment's one-Action ceiling counts full Actions already committed on that actual turn. It blocks a future commitment once one is already committed, while an already-committed second Action finishes. Each actual extra turn has its own ceiling; the source grants no extra turn. Actual extra-Action resources may exist but cannot be newly committed contrary to the active ceiling. Bonus Actions, Reactions, movement and inherent attacks inside one legal Attack Action remain.

The Enchantment DEX rider is exactly -2 Dexterity ability checks/saves EXCEPT initiative; it changes no score/modifier, attack, damage, spell DC or unnamed derived value. AC gets its separate -2 only. Half-Speed uses existing strongest-adverse-Speed arbitration against the shared pre-control Speed, followed by the existing later systemic multipliers. Actual narrowly scoped defenses can suppress/block one component without erasing the others. Neither an Action ceiling retaining the ordinary Action nor Reaction denial claims whole-Action hard control.

Each source keeps its own concentration/save/deadline. Same Slow half-Speed/-2 AC/-2 DEX riders do not add magnitude. Distinct active Enchantment/Transmutation riders can coexist through separate casts; ending one exposes whichever other sources remain, not a merged permanent package.

## Suggestion: task scope and hard-control reservation

NEW binding: Suggestion's persistent mandatory instruction uses its successful establishment timestamp for Compelled Budget Arbitration. It retains that priority while genuinely active, but never supplies an extra budget or overrides an earlier applicable absolute restriction. Actual task permissions and reasonable legal details remain as authored on the card.

If the stated task necessarily requires whole ordinary Actions, including after an awaited conditional trigger, establish and claim the hard component once when Suggestion establishes. Do not reserve afresh per later Action. When blocked, only an independently meaningful legal soft task can establish. That surviving task may replace a prior Suggestion; an attempt with no legal meaningful task does not.

A task established without hard control cannot acquire it dynamically. If changed circumstances require an unreserved whole Action, seek an achievable reasonable path within the original soft permissions, such as waiting for an ordinary door opening. If none remains, end the remaining compulsion. Ordinary temporary delay/inconvenience is not itself cancellation. Neither caster nor target/controller may reword the task to create a new hard permission or extend its original eight-hour deadline.

An actually reasonable hostile task can direct the target's actual ordinary Attack Action/native attack sequence and required mundane ammunition; it does not compel optional finite features, special expendable ammunition, spells/RP or other forbidden expenditures. Reasonableness uses actual target beliefs/loyalties/knowledge/circumstances after payment without a caster diagnostic. ## Scope and open validation

The companion pending-command/phase completions, independent Dominate Beast same-spell records, END-only transition, and Mental Chains voluntary-transport/plane completions on its card have exact manuscript approval.
